**[Flourishing and meaning in life](line/flourishing-and-meaning.md)** (10) — what makes a life go well for the one living it and what makes it meaningful — meaning in life as subjective attraction to what is objectively worthwhile (Wolf), capability and agency freedom against functionings achieved and well-being freedom (Sen), basic needs against what only raises reported well-being, self-realization and its distortions when a life is organized around a proxy for its good, and how arrangements and technologies widen or narrow the lives open to people. Whose a will is stays with authenticity, what organizes efficacy with will-organization, judging an organization with organizational-normativity, and a whole's success against its members' good with distributed-agency (ADR-099):

What the status column means in this scheme — the words are luria's, the meanings are this project's.

| Status | | Means |
|---|---|---|
| `Active` | The current account | The best explanation the record holds for why this happens |
| `Proposed` | Offered | Stated and plausible, on evidence that is suggestive rather than settling — the document says what would settle it |
| `Deferred` | Not yet judged | Filed because the question is real; no position taken on the answer |
| `Rejected` | Disbelieved | Tested and failed, or contradicted by later work — and the thing it explained may still work perfectly well |
| `Superseded` | Replaced | A later account covers the same ground better, and this one names it |

In this record it is the standing caution on every boundary criterion filed beside it ([CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), [CLAIM-161](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md)). It does not say boundaries are arbitrary, only that each is relative to a stated target. | Active |
| [CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md) | Failure of a self to hold together across contexts is a monodromy around a cycle of contexts: any two locally consistent contexts glue, and the minimal model of the obstruction needs three | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-165](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-165.md) ([ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Model contexts (roles, personas, sub-agents) as a cover, and the offsets that reconcile neighbours as a cochain. A global section, one coherent self, exists exactly when the monodromy Φ around a cycle vanishes. Two contexts always glue, so compartmentalization needs a loop. The frustrated XY or Kuramoto energy finds the obstruction: its minimum is 0 exactly when Φ ≡ 0. Abelian case only; re-checked here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) v3 | A candidate structure is worth naming as a unit when its effect-to-noise ratio outruns the Occam cost of keeping it: reify when d'² exceeds the log prior-to-posterior variance ratio, where the model with the candidate stays regular at the parameters that switch it off | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-160](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-160.md) ([ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). By the Savage–Dickey ratio, ln BF(keep) = ½(d'² − Occam), so a direction, block or sector is real enough to name exactly when δ/ε > τ with τ² = ln(s²/σ²), the information the data added about it. In this record it prices the boundary tests for a combined form: a near-decomposable block ([LIT-905](../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)) earns a name when its gap beats its Occam factor. Re-checked here in the conjugate case. Narrowed to candidates whose model stays regular where they are switched off; where it is singular the rule overcharges (CLAIM-188). | Active |
| [CLAIM-155](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-155.md) | Willed agency is a kind between agency and selfhood: a control system whose behaviour is governed by a will-organization over several regimes is more than an agent and closer to a self, in the self-governing sense, without thereby being a subject | The owner's proposal of 2026-10-11, stated with the assistant. Agency can be had without will: a thermostat with its designers, or a training process. A control system that can properly be said to have a will is a narrower kind. It is the jurisdiction of a will-organization, and it is closer to a self in [ADR-024](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md)'s self-governing sense, not in the subject sense. With [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) version 2, it answers the will paper's permissiveness objection on its merits. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-156](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md) v3 | Mindfulness integrates a population of interests by changing which of them may act, and not only by changing what they value: noticing an impulse as an impulse suspends the step from its momentary dominance to its control of action, and that step needs no change in the discount curves | The record's own conjecture, made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. It places mindfulness among [CLAIM-027](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s conditions of efficacy (suspension, accessibility), so it is a second individual-scale instance of that thesis. The one direct study read as summarised ([LIT-906](../../record/literature.d/LIT-906.md)) points the other way, and the claim says so. It does not say mindfulness never changes valuation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md) v12 | Relative to a stated target, a combined form is one system while its joint dynamics are nearly decomposable with the form as a block whose gap beats the Occam factor, and it lasts as long as that block persists; the unit is the gap-isolated block, not any member | The record's proposed answer to [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md), joining the dual-filed MOM results. Simon's near-decomposability says what to compare: interaction inside a candidate block against interaction across its edge. The gap theorem says the unit is the block, and the Occam factor says when the gap is big enough to name it. Persistence is how long the block keeps clearing the threshold. It answers the owner's "privileged nomenclature" for the dancing couple with a test. Proposed: nothing has been measured. One-way drive passes, rightly (CLAIM-167), and the direction of coupling gives the system's architecture. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-158](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-158.md) | Systems differ in whether "who drives?" has an answer at a given level of description, and the kinds form a spectrum: fully top-down, bidirectional, emergent from the whole, and between | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11: "it's probably worth differentiating between systems where 'who drives?' has an answer wrt a particularly level of description or not. I think there's is probably a spectrum/gradient/distribution of kinds here." The record grounds it in the information decomposition ([LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md)), whose downward-causation and causal-decoupling terms separate the kinds, and in proportional causation ([THEORY-133](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md)), which makes a higher level the cause system by system. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-159](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md) v4 | The record's rival accounts of will are claims about drive profiles in different cells: Ainslie's interests are aggregate or emergent, the expected value of control is top-down, and will-organization is the maintained organization that governs how the drive profile changes | The assistant's reading, offered in chat on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's prompt. Ainslie's will has no governor: the person is "just the resultant" of bargaining interests, which is aggregate, or emergent if resolve is a property only the recursion has. The expected value of control posits a dedicated specifying system, which is top-down. The will paper's will-organization is the maintained organization of relations that decides which regime is effective, so it governs the drive profile's changes over time. That is the owner's point that "who drives" is not constant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-160](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) v4 | Data written for a potential future receiver has its intended meaning fixed by the write: even if it is never read, what it was meant to say was settled when it was stored | The owner's claim of 2026-10-11, in their words: "data is written with a potential future receiver in mind. even if the data is never read, its intended meaning was fixed by the write." It separates when identity is fixed (at the write, relative to a projected receiver) from when fidelity is measured (at a read, relative to an actual one), which the line had left unsettled. It does not say what a text means to a given reader is fixed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-161](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md) v2 | A system persists as the same self over an interval when a coherence measure is approximately conserved along its own trajectory, not merely matched by some map between its states | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-153](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-153.md) ([ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The corpus's selfhood condition, that some map φ preserves a coherence score γ, is satisfied by any two systems with similar scores. Requiring the map to be the system's own evolution Φ_Δt makes selfhood approximate conservation of γ along the trajectory: γ is an approximate first integral, and the defect is a number. Proposed here because γ is unspecified. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-162](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) v3 | In flow an activity's immediate reward and its longer-run value coincide, so no interest has to be overridden (synchronization as non-crossing valuations, with no dynamical mechanism claimed), and that is why focused action in flow is reported as effortless | The record's own conjecture, made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. It is grounded only weakly: the effort-cost account is a reading, and the flow literature is registered unread. It says that in flow there is nothing for will to do. It does not say flow is the best or the normal way to act as one. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) v3 | "Synchronization" is an analogy without a mechanism: phase synchrony among coupled oscillators has a coupling, an order parameter and transitions, valuations that fail to cross have none of these, and the word adds nothing to "the curves do not cross" | The record's own anticipated objection to the owner's framing, and the kind [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) found most often real: same structure, not the same mechanism. Superseded on 2026-10-28 by ARG-016, the argument whose verdict it now is. [TERM-050](../../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md) defines synchronization without dynamics, so the claims survive with the word replaced, but then the word is only a name. The body says what would turn the analogy into a mechanism. | Superseded — by [ARG-016](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-016.md) |
| [CLAIM-164](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md) v6 | What a spectral gap makes definite is the subspace of the cluster it isolates, not a single direction: the gap picks the object, and the object is a vector only when its own gap is wide | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-144](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-144.md) ([ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Under a perturbation δT, the subspace spanned by a cluster of singular values separated by a gap δ rotates by at most ‖δT‖/δ (Davis–Kahan), whatever happens to the vectors inside it. So the well-defined unit is the gap-isolated projector. Re-measured here. With [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) it is a criterion: the gap picks the object, and the Occam factor says whether the gap is big enough. | Active |
| [CLAIM-165](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-165.md) v2 | A combined form constituted by mutual entrainment is not thereby a self in the subject sense: two dancers in phase are one coordination, an autonomous process, and still two subjects | The record's own objection to [CLAIM-172](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md), narrowed in version 2 after the owner's reply ([CLAIM-175](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md)). It concedes that the dancing pair is a combined form and an autonomous process. It holds only that nothing in the coupling makes that form a subject, which [ADR-024](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md) reserves "self" for. Open: whether that is the sense of "self" worth asking about is itself in question. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-166](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) v3 | A lower-level collective within the composite person, such as the gut microbiome, can at times drive higher-level behaviour and even experience: the routes exist and the effects are causal in rodents, while the human evidence is modest | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11: "'who drives' isn't a constant. Considering myself as a multi-level agent, part of my composition is my microbiome ... that lower level collective is capable of influencing my higher level behavior and even phenomenological experience." The time claim, the first part, is now [CLAIM-316](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-316.md), split off on 2026-10-15 ([ADR-043](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md)). The microbiome claim is grounded in two reviews read the same day. The routes exist, and the effects are causal in rodents. The human evidence is modest: associations, small effects on subjective stress, and nulls. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-167](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-167.md) | One-way drive rightly passes the threshold criterion: a metronome and its musician, or a nerve and its muscle, form one system relative to a target that needs both, and the direction of coupling gives the system's internal architecture, not its membership | The owner's challenge to the open objection, 2026-10-11: "a metronome driving a musician, or a nerve driving a muscle, passes — and why shouldn't they?" Three reasons, set out by the assistant and accepted for filing by the owner. First, the objection repeats the coupling-constitution worry that [CLAIM-172](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) had already set aside: the criterion makes a new system, not parthood in the organism. Second, its intuitions are about agency, which [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) keeps apart. Third, whether a one-way driver is inside the block or an input is a choice relative to the target. Direction tells peers from hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-168](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-168.md) | Identifying agents by their will-organization is circular: will-organization is defined for an agent already given, and the agent-versus-device comparison presupposes an identified system, so neither can produce the factorization it is meant to find | The record's anticipated objection to the owner's thesis. [TERM-023](../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md) is "agent-indexed": a role in an agent already warranted. The will paper supposes its agent ([CLAIM-080](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-080.md)) so as not to face [CLAIM-010](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-010.md). Orseau et al.'s formal agent-device comparison likewise "assume[s] a clearly identified system". To identify agents by will-organization reverses an order of explanation that was chosen deliberately. Open: [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) replies that the test is run on candidate factors, not on agents. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-169](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md) v2 | On Ainslie's account the population of interests is produced by desynchronized valuation, not given by a fixed architecture: an agent is many interests over a choice only as far as its valuations of that choice cross within the choice's horizon | The record's reading of [THEORY-067](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md), made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. Interests are individuated by the delay at which each dominates, so where curves do not cross there is nothing to individuate them. The self's intertemporal multiplicity is then a variable, not a constant. It does not say that all multiplicity of self is intertemporal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-170](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md) v5 | The agents in a system are a factorization of it relative to a level of description and a target; agents in general are identified by adaptation, and willed agents are individuated by their will-organization: a willed agent is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11, stated in the record's terms after discussion. It is a collaboration, so it is not a quotation: "the agents in a given system are how we factorize that system relative to a given level of description", and agents are "identified by their will (and/or will-organization)". In the discussion, the owner chose will-organization over operative will, in the form "jurisdiction of a will-organization". Operative will flickers with the drive profile; a will-organization is maintained. Narrowed the same day (version 2): agents in general are identified by adaptation, and only willed agents are individuated by their will-organization. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-171](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-171.md) v2 | A stored text means only what its readings make of it: the writer's projected receiver is one more reading, so an unread text has possible meanings and no fixed one | The record's anticipated reception-side objection to the owner's storage claim. Its nearest support in the line is [CLAIM-111](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md), a text supporting a distribution over possible communicative situations. No reception theory is held or read. Open: the reply (the joke changed for the reader, not in what it was made to do) works only if the writer's frame is itself recoverable, and that is [QUESTION-031](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md)'s problem. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-172](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) v10 | Mutual entrainment is a sufficient mark of a combined form, and marks it as one of peers: when each side adjusts the other's timing the pair carries a collective variable neither has alone; one-way drive also makes a combined form, with a hierarchical architecture | The record's reading in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11, "connect extended self to entrainment". Clark & Chalmers' marks of extension are availability marks, and the coupling-constitution objection says coupling does not entail parthood. Mutual entrainment sidesteps the objection rather than answering it: it individuates a new system by its collective variable. It does not cover a passive store like Otto's notebook, which is coupled across time by writing and reading, not by timing. | Active |
| [CLAIM-173](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-173.md) v3 | The threshold criterion measures coupling strength, and coupling is not constitution: a metronome driving a musician, or a nerve driving a muscle, forms a strongly coupled block that clears the threshold without being one system | The record's anticipated objection to [CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md), and Adams & Aizawa's coupling-constitution objection ([LIT-455](../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md)) aimed at the new criterion. Near-decomposability is about the size of couplings, not their direction. One-way drive can make a tightly coupled block. The entrainment claim excluded exactly this case. Rejected on the owner's challenge (CLAIM-167): they should pass, and direction gives a system's architecture, not its membership. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) v8 | A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The assistant's admission test for the owner's thesis, filed at the owner's request. It has three tests on a candidate factor, at a level and for a target. (1) System: it clears the threshold criterion. (2) Description: a model in which it governs its own regimes for goals beats a device model by more than the Occam cost (Orseau et al., priced as in [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)). (3) Adaptation: its governance would change if its actions' consequences changed (Kenton et al.). It answers the circularity objection by running on candidates whose boundaries come from (1), not from agency, and it answers the permissiveness objection without the will paper's supposition. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-175](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md) v3 | A partner-dancing couple, while dancing, is one combined cognitive form on the extended-mind thesis's own terms, more clearly than Otto and his notebook, and merits a name of its own | The owner's reply of 2026-10-11 to the dancers objection, which they had not read: "under extended mind thesis, I'd argue that the pair, while dancing together, comprises a combined form that merits some privileged nomenclature of some kind". Clark & Chalmers endorse socially extended cognition, and the objection's own source calls the interaction an autonomous process. So the objection fails against the combined form and survives only as a question about selfhood. The name is not yet chosen. | Active |
| [CLAIM-176](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md) v5 | Recurrence is the trigger of persistence this record is built around: coding a thing the second time it turns up captures exactly the drift that defeats an argument, and keeps capture from flooding the record | The filing rule of [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) ("a thing gets a code the second time it turns up"), read as one trigger of persistence ([CLAIM-185](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), and the one this record is built around. Narrowed to that on 2026-10-11, on the owner's reframing. The same threshold appears in three places in luria and was found independently each time. Proposed: the rule has been applied, but no other threshold has been compared with it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-177](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) v6 | In the record's exchanges with collaborators who keep no memory, the argument repeatedly loses identity: concepts are redefined silently, objections and readings come back as though new, and the thesis changes without anyone arguing for the change | Stated as a finding in [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md), from seven readers coding the will exchange, and found again in the What Survives Translation? exchange by the workbench reconstructions of 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10. Filed on 2026-10-11 as the first premise of the manuscript. Active since version 2 (2026-10-27), when the body counted six exchanges; the general form beyond one owner and one assistant family is CLAIM-483, Proposed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-178](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) v9 | A manuscript should be a view over the argument and not its only copy: a draft written straight from an exchange drops commitments and changes its thesis without saying so, and both become visible only against a record where claims carry status and inclusion separately | Luria's distinction between sources and generated views, carried over from files to argument. The evidence is the two "crystallized arguments" of the What Survives Translation? exchange and the manuscripts drafted from them (workbench 2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). Proposed: the record is kept beside the manuscript, and nothing generates a manuscript from it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-179](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-179.md) v3 | When an agent does the filing, the cost of capturing argument falls on the party that would otherwise pay to re-derive it, which removes the disparity that design-rationale systems were abandoned over | The answer to the cautionary literature the owner filed before the argument schemes were built ([ADR-030](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md)): design rationale goes uncaptured because whoever captures it is not whoever benefits. [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) noted that agent filing changes the risk from capture stopping to capture flooding. This claim states why. Proposed: the record has run for one week. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-180](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-180.md) v6 | Drift is retrieval failure outside a critical distance: a restatement close enough to an idea retrieves it, one that has drifted too far is taken for new, and a code bypasses retrieval by content altogether | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, when the owner raised sparse distributed memory and Hebbian learning after [CLAIM-182](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md), and filed at the owner's request. It reads the drift of [CLAIM-177](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) through SDM's critical distance (read in [NOTE-242](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md)) and Hopfield's basins of attraction (unread when filed; read 2026-10-14 in NOTE-819). The analogy is the claim; whether restatement distance predicts re-derivation has not been measured. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) v10 | The record fixes the grammar an argument is expressed in, though not its shape: its closed vocabulary of schemes, roles and relations formalizes early, and a move that fits no CLAIM, TERM, ARG or declared relation is forced into one or lost until the misfit is noticed and the grammar amended to hold it | Shipman and Marshall's objection to formal representation ([LIT-756](../../record/literature.d/LIT-756.md)), turned on this record, and narrowed on the owner's correction of 2026-10-11. As the assistant first put it ("a crystal takes the shape of its seed"), it was wrong about crystals. A seed templates the lattice, but the habit is set by growth conditions. The objection therefore reaches the grammar of the argument, and not which claims it comes to hold. Some evidence for it is already in the record: the flourishes it declined to code, and the literature roles that "recurred" but stay in prose ([ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-182](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) v4 | Storage is not anchoring, addressability is: a structure that is kept but cannot be pointed at part by part does not stop re-derivation, and the same content becomes an anchor once its parts get addresses | An answer to [QUESTION-038](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-038.md), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. The evidence is in the record already: the two shared transcripts persisted throughout, and ideas were re-derived inside them anyway. Their moves became citable only when the workbench reconstructions gave each turn a label. Two exchanges, and the comparison is not controlled, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-183](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-183.md) v4 | Generated views of the record, fed back into the exchange, become instruments of the argument: they show where its terms evolved faster than its formalism | From U40 of the translation exchange, the first time a generated view went back into the conversation (workbench 2026/10/10/040455). The assistant read the term-revisions chain as evidence about the manuscript, and made five moves in reply. One of them was "Nucleation itself is a case study". One instance, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-184](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md) v6 | Anchors entrench: a structure that persists early can lock in its framing, so that later structure grows on it and alternatives become hard to reach, and retirement by status is the record's remedy only if superseded anchors stop attracting new structure | The cost side of the owner's reframing ([CLAIM-185](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. If persistence is what lets structure grow, it also lets early framings grow structure that is costly to undo. The test, whether Superseded entries keep drawing new citations, was run on 2026-11-06: they do not (note of that date). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-185](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) v4 | The nucleation threshold of an argument is whatever makes a structure persist: a persistent structure is available as an anchor, and more complex structure can evolve only on anchors | The owner's reframing of 2026-10-11, after two readings showed that no physical nucleation threshold is a count. The threshold is not recurrence as such but whatever triggers persistence. Recurrence is the trigger this record is built around ([CLAIM-176](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md)), and there are others. The readings fit the reframing: a physical nucleus is defined by persistence, and seeds that do not persist lose their power. Proposed: the generalization is stated, not tested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-186](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md) v6 | How fast an argument grows sets how it grows: drift tracks how fast new material arrives relative to how fast it is anchored, so a fast, prolific exchange branches, as a crystal grown far from equilibrium does, and a project memory stabilizes an argument by keeping anchoring up with arrival | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, while correcting its own crystal analogy ([CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md)), and filed at the owner's request rather than on a second occurrence. The analogy is to morphological instability. Near equilibrium a growing crystal faces over, and far from it the faces branch. The evidence so far is anecdotal. The fastest stretch of the translation exchange carried two moves of thesis, and drift has not been measured against pace. There is no slow exchange to compare it with, so the claim is Proposed and untested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-187](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md) v3 | Whether two systems compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the full admissible symmetry group and measuring what remains: a residual barrier marks a different mechanism, and a feature with no counterpart blocks the comparison | The record's one fully measured case of "factor out the admissible symmetries, then test what survives", which the pragmatic-transport line's questions about invariants under admissible transformation ([QUESTION-027](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md), [QUESTION-029](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md), [QUESTION-036](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-036.md)) ask for in the abstract. From five mode-connectivity THEORYs held without links to the line. The carry-over from trained networks to communicative kinds is the filer's, and is the claim's weak point. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-188](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-188.md) v4 | Where the model with a candidate structure is singular at the parameters that switch the candidate off, with real log canonical threshold λ below d/2 and multiplicity m, the reification rule's Gaussian Occam term overcharges keeping the candidate by (d/2 − λ) log n + (m − 1) log log n to leading order, so near the threshold the rule prunes candidates the Bayes factor keeps, and its derivation holds only where that model stays regular | A narrowing of [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), filed on 2026-10-11 from a synthesis review that found the record already held the readings that limit it. [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)'s rule prices a candidate with a Gaussian Occam factor, which is exact in the conjugate case it was re-checked in. The candidates it is meant for (blocks, sectors, couplings with hidden structure) are often singular where they are switched off. There THEORY-087 puts the penalty at λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, not (d/2) log n. On CASE-152's product model the rule prunes, near the threshold, candidates the exact Bayes factor keeps. CLAIM-154 is narrowed to models that stay regular at the switch-off. | Active |
| [CLAIM-189](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) v3 | Fidelity is the wrong measure of a developing argument: maturing drops and changes things legitimately, so what a record can secure is traceability, change that is announced and located, not preservation | The counter to [CLAIM-191](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md), filed with it. The transport line measures fidelity, and [CLAIM-034](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-034.md) already says fidelity is one goal among several. A developing argument aims at maturing, and [TERM-052](../../record/terms.d/TERM-052.md) says maturing drops things legitimately. A fidelity profile would score legitimate dissolution as distortion. What the record secures is that change is announced and located: traceability. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-190](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-190.md) v2 | The anchoring measures are computed in the grammar that shapes the argument, so by themselves they cannot certify that drift fell: drift must also be judged under standards the record did not supply | An evaluation counter to the persistence and growth-rate claims, distinct from [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md). [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) says the record shapes the argument. This says it also shapes the measures. Inbound references per code and turns per anchor are counted in the record's own grammar, so by [CLAIM-149](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-149.md) they cannot also certify that what they encourage reduced drift. Proposed from the synthesis review. | Superseded — by [ARG-028](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-028.md) |
| [CLAIM-191](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) v3 | Restating an argument across memoryless sessions is iterated transport with only a weak channel back to the source: without anchors, restatements drift toward the collaborators' own framings rather than at random, and a code restores continuity of transmission | The first claim joining the nucleating-argument and pragmatic-transport lines, which shared no edges. A sequence of memoryless sessions restating an argument is a chain of retellings, the telephone game of [CASE-015](../../record/cases.d/CASE-015.md). The transport line's results then predict that drift has a direction, toward the transmitters' prior ([THEORY-155](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md), [CLAIM-090](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-090.md)), and that convergence is not preservation ([CLAIM-081](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md)). A code supplies [CLAIM-002](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission. Proposed from a synthesis review; the counter is [CLAIM-189](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-192](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-192.md) v2 | A multi-session argument's thesis can move without any participant arguing for the move, which is a case of an organized whole's course coming apart from its members' intentions | Links the nucleating-argument line to the distributed-agency line. The translation exchange's thesis moved from [CLAIM-017](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-017.md) to [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) to [CLAIM-133](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-133.md) with no turn arguing either move ([CLAIM-177](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md)). [CLAIM-030](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) says an organized whole's operative intention can evolve apart from what its members intend. The owner, the assistant sessions and the record make up such a whole, and its thesis moved that way. [CLAIM-186](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md)'s test is an intervention test of both. Proposed from the synthesis review; the owner's memory and veto are the main reason to doubt it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-193](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md) v5 | A linear probe family can tell apart only realizations whose representations differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed: any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst | A partial answer to [QUESTION-031](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) for the linear case, from THEORYs the record held without linking them to the line. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)); kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed (THEORY-004, THEORY-723); an inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)); and spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). Proved results for learned representations; the carry-over to communicative realizations is the filer's. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-194](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) v7 | A gap or coupling criterion cannot tell a boundary a system produces from one imposed on it: a membrane the cell makes and a beam joining two pendulums pass alike, so the block test cannot by itself supply the individuality minimal agency needs | A counter to the block criterion and to the agency test's first condition, found by two separate reviews of the unlinked THEORYs in the third synthesis pass. It grants the target-relativity [CLAIM-152](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) states. Its point is different: with the target fixed, a near-decomposability gap is a statistic of coupling, and coupling is the same whether the system made the boundary or something else did. [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) and THEORY-1119 place the line at production and self-distinction instead. No case has been measured: the point is that a coupling statistic has no term for who made the coupling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-195](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-195.md) v2 | For an argument, the constraint set that persistence is relative to is fixed by an amendable decision, not discovered: the record stipulates what counts as the same claim persisting, which makes the choice explicit without making it non-arbitrary | Files the point the workbench of 2026-10-11 (214308) left as notes on [CLAIM-185](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) and [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md). Viability is relative to a constraint set the theory does not supply ([THEORY-134](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md)), and the will-organization line leaves "who fixes the constraint set" open ([CLAIM-079](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-079.md), [ARG-007](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-007.md)). For an argument the record fixes it by decision ([ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) and its successors), so the set is explicit and amendable. That shows how one system fixes its set; it does not show the choice is non-arbitrary. | Active |
| [CLAIM-196](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | A person's roles in contexts that do not meet cannot contradict one another: role conflict needs an overlap, which segregating audiences prevents and collapsed contexts create | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Roles in contexts that do not meet glue ([CLAIM-197](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)), so contradiction between them is not yet a failure. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. They segregate audiences, which keeps the contexts disjoint, and they script the occasions where audiences must meet. Broadcast and networked media collapse contexts, which creates overlaps the person did not choose (boyd 2008, after Meyrowitz 1985). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-197](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) v2 | Sections over contexts that do not overlap always glue, so a sense that differs between disjoint contexts is not a gluing failure: a failure needs an overlap carrying sections that disagree, and which families count as covers decides whether anything glues | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-088](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-088.md) ([ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. So "tall", which takes one threshold for people and another for trees, is one global section with the comparison class part of the meaning, not a failure of gluing. A failure needs contexts that overlap and carry sections that disagree there. Which families count as covering is the piece that decides whether anything glues, and a sheaf picture of meaning that does not state it has decided nothing. | Active |
| [CLAIM-198](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. If the windows do not overlap, the sections glue ([CLAIM-197](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)): someone who prefers the diet in the morning and the cake at night is a time-indexed preference, not a divided self. Division needs an overlap, a choice on which both interests bear at once. On Ainslie's account that overlap is made by recursive self-prediction: the present choice is valued as a forecast of the later ones, so the later interest's valuation enters the present context. That is where intertemporal bargaining happens, and it is the coupling [CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-199](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) v5 | Blackwell's order bounds what a rendering makes possible for any receiver, and a given receiver's access is usable information relative to the rules it can apply, which a garbling can raise for that receiver but never above what the source makes possible | The record's reconciliation, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-225](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md). Both standards are kept, in different roles: Blackwell's order is the ceiling, and [TERM-034](../../record/terms.d/TERM-034.md)'s interpreter-relative fidelity ("relative to an interpreter and its available side information") is the receiver's. [CLAIM-087](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md)'s improvement is a gain in usable information. The nearest held reading is [THEORY-176](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)'s "Its loss bounds r's best attainable risk for that problem from above", for restricted rules. The example is checkable; whether real receivers show such gains is a proposal. The usable-information literature was not held when it was filed; Xu et al.'s V-information is now read (note of 2026-10-21). It does not say which rule class real readers have. | Active |
| [CLAIM-200](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-200.md) v2 | The procedure-level fidelity thesis's title says observational fidelity is not defined for a single rendering of a single item, which is more than it shows: one source–target pair does not identify the procedure-level score, and a single rendering can still be judged, as a sample of its procedure or by another measure stated as such, as its own body says | The interlocutor's second refinement at U62 (A240), checked against [CLAIM-228](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s text and granted on 2026-10-10. Version 1's title ended "for a single rendering of a single item it is not defined"; its body says only that this measure does not judge a single rendering, and that one is judged as a sample of its procedure or by another measure. Granted because it can be checked by reading. Repaired in [CLAIM-228](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s version 2, which changes the title only. It does not touch the derivation or the defeat condition. | Superseded — by [ARG-017](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-017.md) |
| [CLAIM-201](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) v2 | Over a fixed scenario, a change of global compatibility at small local distortion needs contextual judgements, which the behavioural data read so far lack; the form of the headline those data leave open is a change of cover, in which a rendering makes some of the source's questions undecidable for its readers and decides others the source left open | The record's narrowing, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-105](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) after [CLAIM-219](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md). It concedes that the record's reading of [LIT-264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) finds no contextual behavioural data, so the fixed-scenario form of "Translation may preserve local meanings while changing the global structure of meaning" has no case but a constructed one. It shows why the fixed-scenario form is sharp and why it needs contextuality. It keeps the form the record already names: "Only a change of scenario can make it jump" ([CLAIM-105](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)), and manuscript §11's "A transport may preserve overlaps but change the available measurement cover". A proposal; its test is the discriminating study. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-202](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md) v3 | What the line adds to functional and relevance-theoretic accounts of translation is measured structure beyond a static pragmatic profile: the context-indexed profile, its response to later framings and its decision relevance predict receivers' recovery beyond the similarity of static stance and footing ratings | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md). This restores [CASE-005](../../record/cases.d/CASE-005.md)'s three-way selection (semantic, static pragmatic and trajectory similarity), which was gone by A52, with human receivers. A proposal, untested. It does not say the functionalist rivals are wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-203](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-203.md) v4 | The only design for the October thesis builds its outcome in: the act is fixed by whoever writes the items, and the topic-only baseline is built to fail on the critical cells | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CASE-040](../../record/cases.d/CASE-040.md) "makes the act a manipulated factor rather than an outcome", so recovering the act recovers the item writer's intent, close to a manipulation check. Its held-out items are built to "break the familiar correlation", so a lexical topic model fails on them by construction. And its baseline is topic-only NMF, not the embedding or surface similarity of [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s own defeat condition. Through [CLAIM-135](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-135.md) it reaches [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s epistemic clause. [CASE-040](../../record/cases.d/CASE-040.md)'s "What it cannot show" covers neither point. | [CLAIM-204](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) v5 | A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization, for which competent participants' uptake is the standard; statistical methods recover aspects of it from restricted observations; translation transports it; and what persists is what the receivers can still recover, of which the analyst can certify the independently identifiable part | The record's restatement, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) after the audit's objections to it ([CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-244](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-206](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), [CLAIM-222](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md), [CLAIM-246](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md), [CLAIM-211](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md)). It supersedes [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. A proposal, not a finding. | Proposed |

It accepts [CLAIM-202](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md) as the line's principal empirical thesis and objects to its rival set. Narrowed and promoted on 2026-10-30, when Nida, Nord and Gutt were read; the baseline it proposed is CLAIM-504. | Active |
| [CLAIM-206](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md) | If a communicative kind can outrun every probe, human same-kind judgements, themselves one probe family, can neither confirm nor defeat the October thesis; if it cannot, the kind does in the tests only what an observational class does, which the record's term for a kind says it is not | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens, with one point from the empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The dilemma reaches the epistemic and fidelity clauses [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) says the programme does test, not only the ontological clause its "What it does not say" sets aside. It does not say kinds are unreal, and it is not [CLAIM-150](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md)'s underdetermination of the ontology. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-207](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md) | The transports of Propositions 1–2 and of D_obs act on judgement outcomes, not texts, and for any one source–target pair a constant kernel transports any overlap-consistent target, so they constrain a translation only once one kernel family is fixed across many utterances and derived from the text channel | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The manuscript's kernels K_C map readers' judgements to readers' judgements, while a translation is a channel on texts, T(v \| u), and [TERM-008](../../record/terms.d/TERM-008.md) records that the two levels are never formally related. It does not say [CLAIM-121](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-121.md) or [CLAIM-070](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-070.md) is false; it bears on what they are used to support. | Active |
| [CLAIM-208](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-208.md) v3 | The compositional predictions are upper bounds whose constants cannot be estimated from serial-reproduction data in a metric fixed beforehand, so the compositional half of the success criterion cannot fail | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The recursion e_n ≤ (∏κ_j)e_0 + Σε_i∏κ_j is a theorem once its constants are the true ones, so a chain cannot depart from it; it can only show a constant was misestimated. A sensitivity κ_i belongs to a reteller's kernel and needs many retellings of each of several inputs at every generation, where a chain gives one. And [CLAIM-059](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-059.md) says amplification "needs a metric other than total variation" (now held as CLAIM-267), so the regime depends on a metric chosen afterwards. [CLAIM-078](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-078.md) records that the compositional half was dropped from the manuscript, not that it cannot fail as stated. It does not say error propagation is unimportant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-209](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-209.md) v2 | Probes and statistical models recover only the distinctions identifiable from the relational evidence they are given, and a signature sufficient for a stated family of communicative decisions outside the observed probes can be identified when the full latent factorization is not | The assistant's second thesis at U62 (A240 T2), the positive answer to [QUESTION-027](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md). It has now been asserted four times: A214 §7, A218 (RQ3 and the priority theorem target), A232 (§3.2 and F2) and A240. Filed with [QUESTION-027](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md)'s scope: the unrestricted claim is answered by standard results, so its content is in decisions outside the observed probes. The claim names no signature; QUESTION-052 names a first candidate, unproved for the directed case (notes of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-30). A proposal; the owner argued none of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md) v2 | Sharing a kind and being a rendering are different relations: kind-sharing is symmetric and says what is to be preserved, while fidelity belongs to a transport from a given source, so an utterance of the same kind made independently of the source shares its kind and has no fidelity to it | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-246](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md). The October thesis puts fidelity in what persists "through those transformations", and [TERM-043](../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) makes fidelity the distortion profile of a transport. So the objection's independent utterance I shares the source's kind and has no fidelity to it, since no transport relates them; the translation T has both. T's provenance is a fact the transport clause supplies, not something the kind criterion must recover. [CLAIM-002](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission concerns the identity of a work, which [TERM-040](../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md) keeps apart from the kind. Active, because it is read off the record's own texts. It does not say judges track descent. | Active |
| [CLAIM-211](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md) v2 | Read as worded, the manuscript's thesis and the October thesis give rival answers to what survives, which come apart in both directions on the cases of the receiver objection, yet the record links them by `complements` and scopes the October thesis to a question its fidelity clause does not stay inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-140](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) shows that the receiver's test and the analyst's identifiability come apart in both directions, and stops at "It does not say the October thesis is false". On those cases [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) and [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s fidelity clause give opposite verdicts on what survived, yet the two are joined by `complements`, which says they answer different parts of one question and do not compete, and [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) answers only [QUESTION-029](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md). Granted: it is a comparison of texts and of the record's relations. It does not say which criterion is right. | Active |
| [CLAIM-212](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md) v3 | Fidelity as a report and fidelity as a re-performance are different decision targets: Blackwell's order compares a rendering with its source as evidence about the source's situation, which both readers decide about, while a rendering that re-performs the act in the target's situation is compared only through a correspondence of situations | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-258](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md), which it reconciles rather than refutes. In report fidelity the parameter is the source's situation, common to both readers, so Blackwell's order is defined; the objection's worked case then gets a precise verdict, incomparability, as [CLAIM-128](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) expects, and a context-aware translator's non-garbling is compared by the order and quantified by [CLAIM-259](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md). The objection is right about re-performance, where [CLAIM-091](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md)'s compensation lives: there a correspondence of situations is needed ([QUESTION-005](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md)). For report tasks the task correspondence is the identity, which removes two of [CLAIM-218](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md)'s points there. A proposal; it does not say which kind of fidelity literary translation aims at. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-213](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-213.md) | A proposed relational kind is a hypothesis about invariance across admissible changes of measurement and context, not an equivalence class under the measurements now available, so realism about kinds gains empirical content as extrapolation to probe families, populations and environments not used to construct them | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12. Proposed and not adopted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-214](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-214.md) v3 | The distribution-over-situations criterion compares each language's own listener posterior, so it needs no correspondence of alternative sets; that a literal rendering can fail it is the criterion detecting a lost implicature, and a target language may admit no rendering that passes | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-236](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md). The objection's worked case is right, and it shows the criterion rejecting a rendering that keeps the literal content and loses a scalar implicature. Active, because it is read off the criterion's form and checked by arithmetic. It does not say the model is right or that the criterion applies to poems. | Active |

The study cannot test it. A proposal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-216](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-216.md) v3 | A thesis that conjoins relational constitution, statistical recovery, transport and receivers' recovery is defeated whole by any one of its empirical findings, though its clauses can hold or fail apart, so the line is better put as separate theses, each with its own defeat condition, resting on one another only where one is a premise of another | The interlocutor's objection at U62 (A240) to the October thesis ([CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)) and to the record's restatement of it ([CLAIM-204](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md)), given as the reason for superseding [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md): "Separates ontology, statistical recovery, and empirical transport instead of making them rise or fall together". Active since 2026-10-30; CLAIM-204 concedes it. It says what would answer it, and does not say an integrative statement is useless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-217](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) v4 | For a communicative kind, the standard of sufficiency is the uptake of competent participants who know the standings and norms in play: a defeasible standard, overridden only where the act's other constituents diverge from the judges' verdicts, so a probe family is tested against it, and a kind outruns the families coarser than that standard and the judges only through those constituents | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-206](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), and the argument [CLAIM-247](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) found missing. For an act partly constituted by uptake ([CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)), competent participants' uptake is that standard, and since version 2 a defeasible one: CLAIM-241 is conceded, so the verdicts yield where the act's other constituents diverge from them. The kind's extension is the class the standard fixes, and analysts' families are insufficient when coarser. No test needs a kind that outruns every family. A proposal, resting on a Proposed premise. It does not touch the ontological clause of CLAIM-204, which superseded CLAIM-139 and keeps that clause, and which the programme does not test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-218](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md) | The task-paired risk difference the record uses in place of Blackwell's order, D_Q = sup_q \|R_q(U) − R_τ(q)(V)\|, is a different quantity: it reduces each risk set to one number, needs the losses of paired tasks on one scale, and its absolute value counts improvement as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-050](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) is stated in Blackwell's order, and the record's decision term is A86's D_Q. A risk per task needs a prior or a minimax summary, where Blackwell's order compares whole risk sets. Subtracting the risks of two tasks needs their losses on one scale, which nothing supplies. The absolute value makes D_Q symmetric, against [CLAIM-106](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md). Granted, because each point is elementary. It objects to [CLAIM-106](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md) by undermining the measure meant to realize it, not [CLAIM-106](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s truth, and it does not say a decision term is unworkable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-219](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) v5 | A change in the global compatibility of a fixed scenario is either a change in contextuality proper, which the behavioural data read show none of, or a change in overlap consistency, which is ordinary context dependence and moves by at most 2ε when each context moves by ε | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala ([LIT-264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)) find no contextuality in five kinds of behavioural data, and [CLAIM-125](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md) reports that 34 of 90 language systems signal too much to be contextual. If pragmatic data are noncontextual as a rule, [CLAIM-105](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s defeat condition is met by default; what is left to change is overlap consistency, which is the "trivial sense of contextuality" and is fixed by the local distributions. The only instance of the headline is the stipulated [CASE-037](../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). Among the claims [LIT-264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) is cited only by [CLAIM-041](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md), not by [CLAIM-105](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md). The objection is open; it does not say a contextual pragmatic data set cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-220](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) v3 | For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the audit's objections to the tests of the manuscript's thesis ([CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-243](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-244](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-226](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md), [CLAIM-222](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md)). It restates [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) as an empirical claim indexed to receivers and tasks, tested against the rival [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) itself names, a proposition with its force, on a behavioural criterion and with an interlingual arm that decides. It supersedes [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. It is a proposal, not a finding. It does not claim the line's distinctive machinery is needed: that is [CLAIM-202](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-221](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) v3 | The relational-constitution thesis's defeat condition describes a standard rival the record holds no counter for, intention-based accounts of illocution, which plausibly meet it for every act in the four-speakers case except the institutional one | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) is defeated by a held account that individuates teasing, reproach and reprimand by the utterance plus speaker-internal states. That is the intention-based line of Grice, Strawson and Bach and Harnish, none of whom the record holds. On it [CASE-018](../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md)'s friend, parent and comedian differ in communicative intention, and only the judge needs norms, which Searle ([LIT-482](../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) already supplies. The objection is open; it would narrow [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) to institutional acts unless an argument from uptake meets it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-222](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md) v2 | No design in the programme includes an interlingual translation, and the defeat conditions are disjunctive, so English retellings and model chains could settle a thesis about what survives translation | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens). The workbench entry for 2026-10-10 notes that the title's question "is left with no translated text in the programme"; no CLAIM says it, and none draws the consequence. Every stimulus set the designs name is English, or names no language; Villon→Henley and Marot→Hofstadter never enter a design. [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s defeat condition ranges over "translations, retellings or cross-modal renderings", so a result on English paraphrase alone can meet it. It does not say intralingual results are irrelevant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-223](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) v2 | Whether a distinction survived is fixed by what the receivers can recover, and whether it can be shown to have survived is fixed by what the analyst's probes can identify, so the manuscript's thesis and the October fidelity clause, read so, answer different parts of one question | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-211](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md), and the argument [CLAIM-140](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) asked for: "the thesis now needs both conditions, or an argument for dropping one". On [CLAIM-140](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s cases: a distinction identifiable but unusable did not survive for those receivers; one usable but unidentifiable survived without evidence of it. Read so, `complements` is right on content. A proposal: it is a reading of [CLAIM-139](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), not what A218 says. | Active |
| [CLAIM-224](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) | Under partial relational constitution, a translation always changes the participants, audience and norms that the relational-constitution thesis makes constituents of the act, so whether the act survives turns on a correspondence of relations the structure cannot supply from inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A translation is addressed to a new audience under new norms, so on [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) it changes constituents of the act, and the record's way out is always a correspondence ("the appropriate relationships", "corresponding relational organizations"). That makes [QUESTION-005](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) a question about what the act is, not only how to measure it, and the record's model of translation holds the audience fixed. [CLAIM-138](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md) spares [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md); this applies its point to [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) through translation. The objection is open. It does not say acts never survive translation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-225](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md) v5 | Blackwell's order measures what an ideal decision-maker could do, not what a given receiver can reconstruct, and the line's claims that a rendering can improve access describe garblings that real receivers do better with, which is the shape of the Blackwell thesis's own defeat condition | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange connects the two claims. A generator that sees only the text makes its image a garbling of the text about the situation, so by Blackwell's theorem the image is no better for any decision. [CLAIM-087](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md) says such an image can improve access. Either that effect is impossible, or judged access is not Blackwell informativeness, and then [CLAIM-050](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s standard is not the one [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s receiver and its defeat condition use. It meets the shape of [CLAIM-050](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, not its letter. It is distinct from [CLAIM-140](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md), which sets the analyst against the receiver: this sets the ideal receiver against an actual one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-226](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) v3 | The defeat tests pool unnamed judges and treat their disagreement as noise, though the theory makes the act partly constituted by its audience; for historical sources there is no source audience at all, and for interlingual ones population differences are read as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A theory on which the act depends on its audience predicts structured variation between judges, so averaging a convenience sample measures an unnamed population's act. The source term of D(τ) for Villon, Henley or Marot can only be a modern reading, and for a live interlingual case the source and target judges are different communities, so the distance confounds population with transport. [CLAIM-074](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-074.md) says fidelity differs across interpreters, as a thesis; it is not applied to the tests. It does not say cross-population fidelity is meaningless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-227](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-227.md) | No validated measure of footing or stance exists in the record, and the one repeated assignment of footing, the analyst's own, changed between passes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Footing and stance are the observables the central theses turn on, yet the only footing judgement made twice of the same texts, the assistant's labelling of its own four refrains, changed between A38 and A39 without comment ([CASE-012](../../record/cases.d/CASE-012.md)), and no design gives judges a definition, a response format, a reliability target or a validation against a known contrast. Granted, because it is a reading of the record. It does not say footing cannot be measured. | Active |
| [CLAIM-228](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md) v4 | D_obs restated over a rendering procedure, with one kernel family fitted on some source items and scored on held-out ones and the target term the readers' response averaged over the procedure's output, separates rendering procedures that receivers' task-indexed recovery separates, so restated it measures observational fidelity informatively | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of the manuscript's L_obs and the profile's D_obs after [CLAIM-207](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md), [CLAIM-230](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) and [CLAIM-235](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md). For one pair a constant kernel makes D_obs zero ([CLAIM-207](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md)); fixed across items, it fits only if the target readers' responses do not vary with the item. The repair ties the outcome-level kernels to the text channel, makes the transport a property of a procedure ([CLAIM-230](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md)), and makes deficiency a finite computation over judgement outcomes ([CLAIM-235](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)). A proposal: the derivation is elementary, but whether the restated measure is informative is the defeat condition's empirical question. It does not say a fitted kernel is the translator's process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-229](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-229.md) v3 | The footing, compensation and constitution theses ground on invented cases whose readings the assistant assigned, and the case filed for the proposition's non-necessity holds the words fixed, so it shows only insufficiency | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-061](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), [CLAIM-091](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md), [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-084](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-084.md) list fictional cases in `grounds`, which [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) makes evidence, while the cases' own bodies say they show a possibility, and [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)'s defeat condition asks a rival to predict a variation nobody observed. [CASE-018](../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md), filed as the necessity half of [CLAIM-061](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), keeps the words fixed, so it shows only that the proposition is not sufficient. Granted: it is a reading of the record. It does not say the theses are false or that invented cases are useless. | Superseded — by [ARG-021](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-021.md), [ARG-020](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-020.md), [ARG-013](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-013.md), [ARG-024](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-024.md), [ARG-039](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-039.md) |
| [CLAIM-230](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) v3 | Blackwell comparison needs the state each rendering is about, which natural texts do not supply, so a decision measure is fixed by whoever labels the state, and it orders translation procedures, not single renderings | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Testing Blackwell's order needs the joint law of the situation and the signal. For natural texts the situation is what interpretation recovers, so it comes from the stimulus design, the analyst's labels or the judges, and decision-relevant information is measured against whoever fixed it. An experiment is a family of distributions, one per state, so a single rendering of a single poem is not one. [CLAIM-050](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, "one rendering is a garbling of another", is then not well typed. It does not say a design-based state is illegitimate. | Active |
| [CLAIM-231](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md) | On observed responses, a rendering that keeps the response distribution of each order of two framings within ε of the source's, under an outcome correspondence, keeps the observed order effect within 2ε, a bound identified from data, while the intertwining identity bounds it only through defects of an unidentified state model | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-253](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md). The commutator identity of the manuscript's §9 holds, and its defects are not identified from data, by the objection's hidden-bit construction. What can be estimated is the response distribution under each order, so the bound is restated on those: a special case of observational distortion with contexts indexed by framing order. Active, because it is elementary and checkable. It does not say the state-model account is wrong, and it does not identify the defects. | Active |
| [CLAIM-232](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md) v4 | Human ratings of stance or footing and human ratings of fidelity of the same renderings share rater construal, scale use and a general impression, which a machine similarity score shares with neither | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Ratings of stance and footing share rater construal, scale use and the reading of one stimulus with ratings of fidelity, and an embedding score shares none of that. The manuscript's split annotators (§10, as [QUESTION-005](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) reports) remove the shared rater, not the shared construal. It is a second reason, beside [CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), that the central tests are easy to pass. Open, because a design could answer it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) v5 | The central theses' defeat conditions pit them only against embedding, propositional or surface similarity, and two rivals the record holds, functional equivalence as Nida states it and a proposition with its illocutionary force, also predict that judged pragmatic observables beat text similarity | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. | [CLAIM-235](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md) v4 | The line's proposed quantities have no finite-data estimators: plug-in signalling from one or a few occurrences per context is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so the contextual fraction is undefined on raw tables, and deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. The plug-in signalling of two empirical marginals is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so raw tables signal, and the contextual fraction is undefined on them. With one occurrence per context, a non-signalling rank-2 system gives Δ of 0, 2 or 4, with expectation 2: the values [NOTE-654](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md) finds in 51 of the 90 systems behind [CLAIM-125](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s "69 of the 90 systems signal". The data are author-assigned corpus senses, not judgements. Deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator. It does not say signalling is rare in pragmatic judgements, where order effects are themselves signalling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-236](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md) v2 | Under the rational-speech-act model the distribution-over-situations thesis grounds on, a form's interpretation depends on what else the speaker could have said, so matching source and target posteriors needs a correspondence of alternative sets that translation changes and no entry names | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. | [CLAIM-237](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-237.md) v3 | The first open problem of directed transport is not yet posed: a contextual model is a menu of incompatible experiments, and under the natural order on menus any state-independent classical simulation is dominated automatically, so what is open is only the converse or a deficiency bound | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Blackwell's order compares experiments, each a family of distributions over one parameter. Posing [CLAIM-125](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s first part needs models indexed by situations and an order on menus of experiments. Under the natural order, the preservation direction is automatic for a classical simulation that does not depend on the situation. Granted, because the argument is elementary. It narrows what is open; it does not close it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-238](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md) v3 | Many of the line's defeat conditions cannot in practice be met: the comparative ones are null results with no margin over an observable set the thesis may re-choose, and the possibility theses' are universal negatives that no finite study establishes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it, though [CASE-029](../../record/cases.d/CASE-029.md) records the decision rules that were dropped.
