A two-variable process with nothing hidden shows it is not enough: a acts on b within one step, a is Granger-noncausal for b, and setting a(t) changes the mean of b(t + 1) by ργ. Checked by hand and by simulation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-334](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md) | Granger causation from a macro variable to the micro variables it supervenes on, Seth's downward Granger causation, is not evidence of a macro-to-micro intervention effect, even with every micro variable measured: supervenience leaves no intervention on the macro variable that holds its micro base fixed at the same time | Seth measures downward causation as Granger causation from the flock's centre of mass to each boid, and calls it "ontologically innocent" ([THEORY-703](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-703.md)). The record files the boundary so that the stronger reading has an address. Measuring every boid does not help, by [CLAIM-333](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md). | Active |
| [CLAIM-335](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md) v4 | Transfer entropy measures directed predictive improvement, not information flow: as a conditional mutual information it is the source's unique information about the target's next value plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a source with a bit the source carries only jointly and read zero from sources that jointly fix the target, and conditioning on more series does not remove the synergy | The record's position on whether transfer entropy measures information flow. Williams and Beer's decomposition shows why, for any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations ([THEORY-712](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md)). Both papers' examples were recomputed exactly. This is a different failure from [CLAIM-333](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md)'s, prediction against intervention. It leaves transfer entropy standing as a predictive quantity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-336](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) v11 | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". | [CLAIM-337](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) v2 | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. Sandved-Smith et al. cast mental action as policy selection over higher-level cognitive states; Brouillet and Friston make felt fluency an inference about the precision of one's own processing; Smith et al. let a generative model grow its own structure by inference and learning alone. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. A redescription with no action on the world concedes that action on the world is not part of the loop. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-338](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v5 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." Worked out by A10. Selective sampling is the β arrow of [CASE-099](../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), authority shaping interpretation through what it retrieves. Policies scored on current beliefs are the γ arrow. So Friston's agent runs both arrows, and his "this weakness becomes the strength" accepts capture, with the anchor moved outside the loop to selection on whole agents. The sharp edge: the mapping relocates sampling from the world to retrieval, which is [CLAIM-337](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md)'s move reversed, and it holds only if the agent's own store can surprise it as the world can. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-339](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-339.md) v3 | A judgement–observation loop cut off from action loses one route for evidence it did not select, and the free-energy principle's reason for minimizing surprise, that a persisting system must keep its states in bounds, needs action on the world, though a loop can confirm itself with action available too | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, narrowed at A4. Friston et al. (2010) say active sampling is "mandated by ergodic arguments based on the very existence of adaptive agents", and the enactive account puts a system's own norms in its capacity to act against tendencies toward its viability boundary. Kübler and Birbaumer's extinction hypothesis is the empirical form. As first filed it said a loop without action has a self-confirming minimum. [NOTE-766](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) shows the minimum arises with action available, so the counter now claims only that losing action removes one source of evidence the loop did not select. [CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) answers it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-340](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) v2 | Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to conferral has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose | The formal question [QUESTION-121](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) asked, answered in [CASE-099](../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s linearization ([CASE-106](../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md)): is committing predictions before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? No. The coupling γ is 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄), where κ̄ is how far the shared meaning bends the committed predictions and κ′ how far it bends the reading of the evidence. It is corrective, null or capturing as κ′ is below, at or above κ̄. Strong correction can fail by oscillation when \|βγ\| ≥ 1 − αδ. | [CLAIM-341](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) v5 | The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active | The owner's, U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: Friston's free-energy approach is "generally correct, but the cybernetic model is wrong"; action can be cut out of the loop, which decomposes into "Judgement (qua measurement that generates interpretations) <--> Observation". At U2 the owner held that the pragmatic-transport and will-organization models are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The claim is stated in that model's terms, as [CLAIM-297](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and in the diachronic form A4 proposed and the owner asked to be filed at U5 ("make the revisions"): a judgement need not produce the observation it judges, but it reshapes the observer that produces the next one. | [CLAIM-351](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) v3 | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." | [CLAIM-357](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v9 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility need not be the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". | [CLAIM-365](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The sharp edge: it says what to start from, not that a frustrated organization is distressed or feels anything. | [CLAIM-369](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v5 | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. Mehta et al. (2019) and Marsland, Cui and Mehta (2020) give the general duality for consumer–resource models. | Active |
| [CLAIM-370](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md) | For a symmetric positive-pair distribution with marginal p, the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p) has the density ratio K⁺ as its kernel, and it is Hilbert–Schmidt exactly when the χ²-divergence of the pair from the product of its marginals is finite, in which case it is compact and self-adjoint with an orthonormal eigenbasis | [THEORY-005](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md)'s derivation, stated as the record's own and with its proof. Johnson et al. ([LIT-258](../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md)) write the operator on a finite space without an integrability condition. HaoChen et al. ([LIT-249](../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md)) reach the Hilbert– Schmidt property from a uniform bound, which is stronger. Here the condition is exact: Hilbert–Schmidt if and only if finite χ². It says nothing about what trained features span. | Active |
| [CLAIM-371](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-371.md) | Under the componentwise order on distortion profiles, two profiles are incomparable exactly when they trade off, and then positive weightings can rank them either way, while every positive weighting agrees with a dominance | The order-theoretic part of [CLAIM-128](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md), on its own so that it can carry its own warrant. Only that, under the componentwise order of [TERM-043](../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md), a trade-off is incomparability, that a trade-off can be resolved either way by positive weights, and that a dominance cannot. | Active |
| [CLAIM-372](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Within a fixed measurement scenario, the contextual fraction is a piecewise-linear and Lipschitz-continuous function of the empirical model's probability table, with a constant that depends only on the scenario | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. The non-contextual fraction is the minimum of the dual objective over finitely many vertices, so it is concave and piecewise linear in the probability table, and the contextual fraction is Lipschitz in it. The constant is the largest ℓ₁ norm of a dual vertex, which depends only on the scenario and is not bounded here. Nothing here crosses scenarios or applies to signalling data. | Active |
| [CLAIM-373](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-373.md) | If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖ | The commutator-distortion identity of the manuscript's §9, on its own and proved. A map that nearly intertwines each of two operations carries their commutator to the commutator of the images, up to an error that is linear in the two intertwining defects. [ARG-006](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-006.md) is the exact case. It says nothing about whether the defects can be identified from data ([CLAIM-253](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md)), or what bounds an observed order effect ([CLAIM-231](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-374](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-374.md) | On a consistently connected system, Contextuality-by-Default and the sheaf criterion agree: a maximally connected coupling exists exactly when a global law has the contexts' laws as its marginals | The record's derivation of what [NOTE-600](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md) marks as its own inference. In a consistently connected system, every observable has one distribution in all the contexts that contain it. Then each connection's maximal coupling makes its copies equal with probability 1 ([LIT-777](../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3), so a maximally connected coupling is a joint law of one variable per observable, which is a global section in Abramsky and Brandenburger's sense ([LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md), [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)). Conversely, a global section gives such a coupling. The two criteria come apart only when marginals shift with context. | Active |
| [CLAIM-375](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) v4 | Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that grants influence to an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the grant scheme hold together | The demonstrated core of [CLAIM-285](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md). Under A3's one-hop rule I_j = I_j⁰ + Σ_(k≠j) b_k E_kj, with budgets and baselines fixed within an epoch ([CLAIM-282](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)), an operator's authority does not respond to its own grants. If the collective decision is the authority-weighted mean of the operators' policies, then granting influence to an ally whose policy is nearer one's own than the decision is moves the decision strictly toward one's policy. So the reward for realized policy, and not for held authority, pays for delegating. It does not say operators behave so, or that any rule beyond one hop keeps both conditions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-376](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) v2 | A linear system that is stable at every instant can have a positive Lyapunov exponent: shifting any operator with exponent λ > 0 by −δI lowers its exponent by exactly δ and makes every instantaneous operator stable, so for 0 < δ < λ the shifted system is stable at every instant and unstable | The case [THEORY-724](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. If A(t) has first Lyapunov exponent λ > 0, the propagator of A(t) − δI is e^(−δt)Φ(t), so its exponent is exactly λ − δ, while every eigenvalue of every A(t) moves left by δ. Applied to the undamped oscillator switching ω between 0.5 and 3 every unit of time: λ = 0.1955, and with δ = 0.1 the system is stable at every instant, with eigenvalues −0.1 ± 3i and −0.1 ± 0.5i, and has exponent 0.0955. | Active |
| [CLAIM-377](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | For any differentiable model under squared loss with Gaussian noise of precision β, the model's Fisher on n inputs is the Gauss–Newton matrix βJᵀJ, and its non-zero eigenvalues are exactly β times those of the empirical NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ, with the same multiplicities, its eigenvectors being Jᵀ applied to the Gram matrix's, normalized | [THEORY-084](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-378](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) v2 | A representational similarity index invariant to every invertible linear map depends on a representation only through its column space, so it takes one value on all column-centred representations of rank n − 1, as it does on all representations of rank n | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |
| [CLAIM-379](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) v2 | On a finite set of stimuli, regularized linear readouts with ridge b > 0 cannot tell apart two centred representations of the same width exactly when one is an orthogonal transformation of the other, and the unregularized CCA member cannot tell apart representations with the same column space, which differ by an invertible linear map | The proved core of [CLAIM-269](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md). What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of K_X = X G⁻¹ Xᵀ/M, with G = aC_X + bI ([THEORY-008](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). For b > 0, K_X and the Gram matrix XXᵀ determine each other, by a monotone map on the shared eigenvalues; and equal Gram matrices mean an orthogonal transformation ([CLAIM-290](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md), [THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). For b = 0, K_X is the projection onto the column space, which fixes X only up to an invertible linear map, as for a softmax layer ([THEORY-723](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-380](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-380.md) v2 | With finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source, and has A86's D_Q as its symmetrization | The finite-outcome part of [CLAIM-326](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior. A garbling never gains. The term is directed. A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-381](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Over a finite class of items with finite judgement outcomes, a constant outcome kernel fits every item only when the target readers' averaged responses do not vary with the item, an exact fit is a garbling with the item as common parameter, and Le Cam's deficiency and its restriction to finitely many decision problems are finite computations | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. | [CLAIM-382](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) v2 | In an autoencoder initialised with i.i.d. Gaussian weights and zero biases and trained by SGD or momentum SGD on a loss of its output, the law of each hidden layer's learned representation is invariant under every orthogonal map of that layer that commutes with its activation, so under a radial activation no basis is privileged in law, while elementwise tanh or Leaky-ReLU yields invariance only under the signed permutations or the permutations, which leaves the standard axes free to be privileged | [THEORY-288](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. | [CLAIM-383](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) v3 | In plane Couette and plane Poiseuille flow, measured in the energy norm, the linearized operator about the laminar profile has transient growth at least cR and resolvent norm at least cR² with c independent of R, so wherever it is eigenvalue-stable a perturbation of norm at most CR⁻² makes it eigenvalue-unstable | [THEORY-304](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. The sharp constants, and that the growth is no more than order R, come from the computation and are not here. | Active |

| [CLAIM-388](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v5 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". | [CLAIM-391](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-391.md) | For any classes with weights π_c and per-class factor matrices H_c and Δ_c, the class-wise Kronecker product Σ_c π_c H_c ⊗ Δ_c exceeds the product of the weighted averages H̄ ⊗ Δ̄ by exactly the weighted between-class covariance Σ_c π_c (H_c − H̄) ⊗ (Δ_c − Δ̄), so the two agree when either factor is the same in every class |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-393](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s defeater counts a test-passing factor that is "by independent marks, not an agent". | [CLAIM-394](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-394.md) v2 | In a stationary linear Gaussian VAR(1) that is time-reversible (AΠ = ΠAᵀ, Π the stationary covariance), every slow-feature direction is a left eigenvector of A, so any span of slow features is an exactly dynamically independent coarse-graining; off reversibility a slow feature is in general neither independent nor free of memory | Derived in the reading of Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [NOTE-1015](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-395](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-397](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md) v2 | For a scalar stationary process with autocovariance C, the Mori–Zwanzig memory kernels for the projection onto the current value are fixed by C alone, through C(m+1) = Σ_{k≤m} c_k C(m−k); the memory vanishes iff C is geometric, and when C has finite Hankel rank d the memory has Hankel rank exactly d − 1 | Derived in the reading of Lin and Lu (2019), [NOTE-1029](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md), and re-checked here. Scalar Y, VAR(1), Gaussian noise. | Active |
| [CLAIM-399](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-399.md) | Causal abstraction in the senses of Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern does not secure governance-response sufficiency: exact transformation, τ-abstraction and zero approximate-abstraction distance all accept the hidden-bit coarse-graining, which loses ρ(h = 1) bits of the response to h, because each lets high-level noise carry what the coarse state drops; for one outcome and the identity correspondence, sufficiency is their compatibility condition with the high-level context fixed to the coarse state, and strong abstraction rejects the case only through interventions on the hidden parameter | The record's join, on 2026-10-21, of its readings of the causal-abstraction papers ([NOTE-1037](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), [NOTE-1032](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), [NOTE-1045](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md)) with [CLAIM-407](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). A25 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "We should not present governance-preserving coarse-graining as a new general theory of causal abstraction." That stands. But it is not an instance of these papers' notions either: their criteria compare interventional laws and let the high-level context be any map that works, so they accept the hidden governance bit, whose coarse state keeps nothing of the response to h. | [CLAIM-400](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v6 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or conferral (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. | [CLAIM-401](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v5 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). | [CLAIM-403](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) v10 | A contribution's admission to an organization's inquiry, its recognition in apt terms, its credibility, its uptake into judgements, and its contributor's part in revising the standards of uptake are separable, each possible without the later ones, so an organization can widen access while every channel by which a less authoritative contribution could change the criteria of authority stays closed | A24 §6 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U24: "Someone's contribution may be received and politely acknowledged yet have no mechanism through which it can change institutional understanding." | [CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) v15 | An organization can be governed from outside without any of its decisions being made for it, through the evidence its own procedures receive or through the criteria by which they weigh evidence; the two routes are distinct and each is possible without the other, so informational and evaluative independence do not imply each other; and where the organization's role is to evaluate another that affects its evidence or resources, the interpretation–authority loop can close between the two institutions, so that formal independence of the evaluator's procedure does not make its evaluation independent | The owner's cases, U20 ("maybe cases like reflexive control and regulatory capture could be informative here") and U21 (news-media capture) of the exchange of 2026-10-20, with A26 §4's two constructions and A27 §6. | [CLAIM-431](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) v4 | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. | [CLAIM-469](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md) v5 | Luria is an apparatus for a record's objects in the operational sense: through its schemes, vocabularies, validators and generated views it realizes a system of distinctions that fixes what counts as a referable and governable object within the record, so that a split scheme makes one object two and a promoted vocabulary makes a value an entity; it keeps, enforces and propagates those distinctions; and its distinctions are revised through the record's own use | The operational half of [CLAIM-476](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md), split from it at the owner's review of the pull request. | [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) v8 | From interconnection to individuation, the relationships are distinct achievements that form a partial order, not a nested sequence: none implies the next, and a later one need not require every earlier one. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 as SYNTHESIS-006 ([ADR-077](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated, and returned to CLAIM under its own code on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084). | Active |
| [CLAIM-475](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) v13 | Specifying is itself a resource-bounded realization: formulating a question takes time, concepts and computation as realizing a configuration takes energy and matter, so the questions an agent can ask are a product of what it has already realized; a stabilized specification is past inquiry stored so that later questions become cheaper to ask, and it can make other questions harder | The owner's, U17 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "resource constraints impact specification in exactly the same way as they impact realization. A stable specification amortizes the work that made it, which is a separation of time scales ([CLAIM-478](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)), and entrenches what it makes cheap. | Active |
| [CLAIM-476](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md) v5 | Beyond what it does operationally, luria is an apparatus in Barad's constitutive sense for the objects of a record, and only for them: the record's objects are constituted, and not only made referable and governable, by the distinctions its grammar enacts, so that the same authored material is a different set of objects under a revised apparatus, and the record's own inquiry reconstitutes the apparatus that constitutes them | The owner's, U7 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "oh shit, I think I may have inadvertently operationalized this notion of apparatus already, check out github.com/dmarx/luria". That needs an argument the operational facts do not supply, and the readings press on it, since Barad rejects carrying agential realism as a template. Of Barad, only her 2012 essay is read here (NOTE-1458), and it gives no general account of an apparatus. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-477](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md) v3 | Relata stand to relations as realizations stand to specifications: what an entity is, is partly fixed by the constraints on the configurations of entities and relations it can enter, and those constraints are themselves realized and maintained by something, so neither relata nor relations, nor specifications nor realizations, are prior without qualification | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, "maybe relata:relations::realization:specifications/constraints?", after U6 had set the record's ambitions as "extremely abstract and unrestricted". | [CLAIM-478](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md) v6 | Rate differences help make structure and not only mark it: where some degrees of freedom settle faster than others by more than the rates vary among them, the relation they settle into is a constraint on the system over the window between the two rates, so what is a realization at one rate works as a constraint at another; and organization can make new rate differences in turn, as when modes slow near an instability and become order parameters, so hierarchies of rates and constraints can produce one another | The owner's, U12 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "I think we may still have a coverage gap wrt scale separation and how that participates in creating structure". A12 agreed and found that the gap was synthesis, not literature: the record held [CLAIM-331](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), [CLAIM-327](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), [THEORY-661](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md), [CLAIM-395](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) and Mori–Zwanzig readings. It goes beyond [CLAIM-331](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), on which slowness is a mark of a level, in two ways: separation makes constraints, and constraints can make separation. It supplies the mechanism for [CLAIM-477](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)'s recursion. | [CLAIM-479](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-479.md) v2 | In the record a typed relation is more constrained than either of its relata: a claim's content is open prose, while `rests_on` fixes the scheme at both ends, has `supports` written as its converse and says what retiring its target leaves, and none of that moves when either claim's content does; so a relation's rigidity is a fact about the grammar, not evidence that the dependency it records is sound | The owner's, U6 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, against A5's "its relationships are explicitly represented rather than metaphysically primitive": "and yet interestingly, relations like "supports" are less flexible than the raw contents of either relata." Shown from luria.yaml, which A6 §6 read correctly. [CASE-131](../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) is the instance in which the rigidity of a relation outran what its relata meant and the grammar was amended. | Active |
| [CLAIM-480](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composing interactions can turn an interior into a constraint, and sometimes into a constraint of a new kind: in the chain E = ½k₁(x₁ − x₂)² + ½k₂(x₂ − x₃)², with x₂ internal and equilibrated, the boundary sees E_eff = ½·k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)·(x₁ − x₃)², a coupling between x₁ and x₃ that neither part has; if the interior relaxes slowly, eliminating it leaves a history-dependent constraint, a memory kernel, so interconnection fixes an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories and separation of time scales decides only whether that constraint is approximately memoryless; and for cellular sheaves the reduced constraint can relate three boundary values where every relation among the parts is pairwise | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." Baez and Fong's black-boxing functor is the general theorem for passive linear networks. The memory case ties it to Mori–Zwanzig and to [CLAIM-478](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md): interconnection yields an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories in every case, and separation of time scales decides only whether it is approximately memoryless. For cellular sheaves the reduction can need a richer relational vocabulary than the parts used (THEORY-1090; QUESTION-283). It is independent evidence for [CLAIM-477](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md), that constraints are realized by organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-481](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md) v4 | Coupling does not by itself separate time scales: two identical undamped oscillators coupled with stiffness k have normal modes at ω₀ and √(ω₀² + 2k), nearly equal when k ≪ ω₀², and neither decays; separation comes where the coupling dissipates relative differences faster than collective ones, as in ẋ = −ax − k(x − y), ẏ = −ay − k(y − x), whose collective and relative modes relax at rates a and a + 2k, and in a Laplacian flow ẋ = −κLx, where the spectrum of L sets the rates | The answer A20, A21 and A23 gave to the owner's conjecture at U20 that coupling necessarily induces scale separation ([CLAIM-473](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md)). Two small computations: conservative coupling splits modes without separating or damping them, and dissipative coupling damps the relative mode at a rate that grows with the coupling. For a Laplacian flow the kernel is exact compatibility and the nonzero spectrum is the hierarchy of relaxation rates, so a spectral gap is where the separation comes from. Conceded, so Active. It gives a mechanism for [CLAIM-478](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s second half and is not a test of individuality. | Active |
| [CLAIM-482](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-482.md) v2 | An organization's aggregate revealed preference exists exactly when its record of winning moves never cycles, and where it exists it is fitted to one regime of authority, so an intervention on authority that changes the winning moves changes the fitted preference and the preference does not predict the change | The status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) found the record's later formal work bearing on an objection it never cited. [CLAIM-089](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-089.md)'s aggregate version says Northstar "simply prefers speed": the governing relations are the organization's revealed preference. [CLAIM-434](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md), Active and demonstrated, says when such a preference exists: an ordering that every winning move climbs exists exactly when the wins never cycle. So the objection is not refuted in general. It is true of an organization whose record is acyclic, and unavailable for one whose record cycles. Where it holds, the ordering is read off the wins under one regime of authority. [CASE-003](../../record/cases.d/CASE-003.md) changes authority and holds attitudes and evidence fixed, and the wins change. Then the fitted ordering changes too, and nothing in the first ordering predicted the second. The revealed preference redescribes the outcome of the governing relations, which is the reading [CLAIM-027](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s defeater excludes ("whose content predicts the outcome"). | Active |
| [CLAIM-483](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-483.md) | An argument developed with collaborators who keep no memory fails mainly at identity and not at structure, so that coding what recurs, not argument mapping, is the remedy, and this holds beyond one owner and one assistant family | The comparative and general half of [CLAIM-177](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) version 1, split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) and kept Proposed. [CLAIM-177](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) now says what the record observed: identity failures recurring across six exchanges with one owner and one assistant family. Whether they outnumber structure defects was counted in one exchange only, and the population is one owner and one family, which [CLAIM-177](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md)'s own body called "a pattern, not a measurement". | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-484](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-484.md) v3 | Internal conflict is the gap between the precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it | The second half of [CLAIM-283](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) version 1, split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) and kept Proposed. Each of [CLAIM-283](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md)'s four dependents ([CLAIM-368](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md), [CLAIM-440](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md), [CLAIM-442](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-442.md), [CLAIM-446](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md)) uses only the first half, the distinction between claimed precedence and granted authority, which is now [CLAIM-283](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) and is Active. That internal conflict is this gap is a further identification, and no case in the record shows it. [CASE-151](../../record/cases.d/CASE-151.md) and [CASE-127](../../record/cases.d/CASE-127.md) illustrate the separation of access from authority, and their notes say they do not show that a motive claimed precedence. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-485](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) v2 | In the self-governing sense, what endogenous governance adds over a behaviourally equivalent system with an external scheduler is not that it allocates authority among its own processes but that it can revise its own governing standards when they break down | The bridge the owner asked for on 2026-10-28, between Kahl's proposal (THEORY-1165), which is about agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, and [QUESTION-092](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md), which fixes [TERM-045](../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s sense 5, self-governing. It is the record's answer to the question. Internal allocation of authority, the second of [CLAIM-025](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s separable capacities (governing among regimes), coordinates execution and does not make a system govern itself more than an external scheduler would. The capacity to revise its governing standards when they break down does: the third capacity, which [CLAIM-284](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) names as taking part in governing the conditions of its own transformation. Two systems matched within a regime differ under it, and they diverge in behaviour once that regime breaks down. | Active |
| [CLAIM-486](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-486.md) v2 | A rendering can keep the communicative act while changing the proposition, so preserving the proposition is not necessary for preserving the communicative event | The necessity half of [CLAIM-061](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md)'s version 1, split off when the status review of 2026-10-28 narrowed [CLAIM-061](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md) to sufficiency ([ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). Its one documented case is Phillips's handshake for Paul's holy kiss ([CASE-056](../../record/cases.d/CASE-056.md)), which competent judges took to keep the greeting. The defender of necessity has a reply the record does not answer: the proposition worth keeping is the coarser one, and the handshake keeps it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-487](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-487.md) | Describing the relations that decide which regime becomes effective as one will-organization, across realizers, explains something that planning theory, control theory, executive-control research and institutional theory each describing their own realizer does not | The explanatory-gain claim the paper stakes itself on, filed separately by the status review of 2026-10-28. It was carried by [CLAIM-027](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s standing without being one of its words, so [CLAIM-024](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)'s objection had no target of its own. [CLAIM-021](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-021.md) concedes the mechanisms; this is what is left to show: that one description across realizers earns its keep. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-488](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-488.md) v3 | Le Cam deficiency, after Torgersen, would quantify the approximate case of the Blackwell order for translation, and decoder-only audience knowledge would make the coding problem a Wyner-Ziv problem | The two steps of the manuscript's §5 that [CLAIM-050](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) carried until the status review of 2026-10-28 and that rest on works the record has not read: deficiency for the approximate case (Torgersen) and the Wyner-Ziv form of decoder side information. Split off when [CLAIM-050](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) was narrowed to what its read sources support ([ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). | Active |
| [CLAIM-489](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-489.md) v2 | A sign's communicative significance is fixed by its contrasts within a system rather than by correspondence to a referent | [CLAIM-082](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s version 1 title, kept as its own Proposed entry when the sixth status review narrowed [CLAIM-082](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md) to what Saussure's value supports ([ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). It carries the two parts the reading does not: that significance in use is fixed this way, and that contrast works instead of reference rather than alongside it. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-490](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md) | A fanbase is a mixture of spectators who relate to the club in different ways, as supporters, followers, fans and flâneurs, so the public stance credited to it is weighted towards the most committed types before any bias in who is sampled | From Giulianotti's taxonomy ([THEORY-1111](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md)): supporters are hot and bound to the club as community, while flâneurs are cool consumers who switch clubs. The expressions that make up "the fans hate the owner" come from the hot types, and the cool ones take no part. So the stance is the committed segment's by composition, before amplification or preference falsification. It does not say the committed segment is a minority, or that its stance is illegitimate. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-491](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) v6 | No action is selfless in the sense of aiming at a good that is no self's: what is called selflessness, collectivist or altruistic, is concern for the good of a self extended to include others or a group, so collectivism is self-interest on a larger self-identity | The owner's position, from the discussion that raised self-categorization theory (2026-10-28 and 29). Selves come at more and less inclusive levels: social identity in self-categorization theory, fusion, self-expansion, interdependent self-construal. Apparent selflessness is then concern for a larger self. Cialdini et al.'s "oneness" result is its best evidence; Batson et al.'s rejoinder and the risk of trivial truth are its objections. It does not say people are self-centred, or that groups have no good of their own. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-492](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-492.md) v2 | If the self is defined to include whatever an agent cares about, the claim that all motivation serves the self is true by definition and rules nothing out; the thesis has content only with a criterion of the self's extent that can come apart from what the agent cares about | The classic objection to psychological egoism (Butler; Sober and Wilson, [LIT-1683](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)), turned on the owner's thesis. "Every motive is my motive" is trivially true and does not make every motive self-interested. "My self includes whatever I care about" makes the thesis unfalsifiable. It is answered if the thesis names an independent criterion of the self's extent, such as overlap, fusion or salient self-categorization, and predicts that motivation follows that criterion and not caring alone. | Active |
| [CLAIM-493](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-493.md) v2 | When a fanbase is set against an outside party such as its club's owner, its more extreme members become more prototypical of it, so a vocal minority can fix the fanbase's public stance through a group process and not only through biased sampling of who speaks | A derivation from self-categorization theory: in an intergroup context the more extreme members of a group gain prototypicality (Turner et al. 1994, p. 458, reporting Haslam and Turner). If influence follows prototypicality (Turner 2005, unread), a fanbase opposed to its owner will treat its most hostile members as most representative. A minority stance can then become the fanbase's public stance by a group process that A2's preference falsification and amplification do not need. It does not say that the private majority agrees. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-494](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-494.md) v2 | Empathic concern for another produces motivation whose ultimate goal is the other's welfare, and it does so when perceived self–other merging is controlled, so not all helping is concern for an extended self | The empathy–altruism hypothesis as Batson et al. (1997) defend it against Cialdini et al. (1997): in experiments (two, by the SEP's account), empathy predicted helping with self–other merging controlled, and merging did not mediate it. Sober and Wilson (1998; [LIT-1683](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)) argue on independent grounds that psychological egoism is not established. Filed as the empirical objection to the owner's thesis; both papers are unread, so the record holds the disagreement, not its resolution. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-495](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-495.md) | For an O(d)-valued connection on a connected graph, the assignments that meet every edge relation xᵢ = Tᵢⱼxⱼ form a space isomorphic to the vectors at one vertex fixed by every holonomy based there, which is the kernel of the connection Laplacian; for d = 1, and for U(1) phases, that space is all or nothing, but for d > 1 a connection whose loops are not trivial can still keep a subspace on which every loop is, so compatibility among local frames can be partial and graded by direction; and edge maps that do not commute can compose to a flat loop, so non-commutativity is not holonomy | From A2 and A3 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), which drew it out of [LIT-1820](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s O(d) setting against [THEORY-1082](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md)'s U(1) one. The proof and the example are the record's, checked numerically. It is the zeroth cohomology of the connection sheaf, so standard, and it says nothing about which organizations have such transports. | Active |
| [CLAIM-496](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md) | Agreement between routes of translation is a measure of coherence, not of fidelity, and the two are independent: a rendering that sends every source utterance to one output makes direct and relay transport agree exactly while a receiver who could tell a promise from a prediction with no error is left at chance, and two routes that keep the act and differ in register disagree completely while losing nothing the act-identification task needs | From A4 and A5 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), where the assistant carried [LIT-1820](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s comparison of alternative paths over to translation and then warned that "path agreement is a coherence criterion, not a fidelity criterion". The constructions are the record's. It does not say path discrepancy is uninformative: it says it measures something [CLAIM-259](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s directed loss does not, and conversely. | Active |
| [CLAIM-497](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-497.md) v2 | A system's causes are found at the coarsest description whose interventions are unambiguous: a macro description is causally proportionate where it merges only micro states that intervention cannot tell apart, and no coarse-graining carries more causal information than the micro description it supervenes on | The record's position on causal emergence after [THEORY-787](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) was rejected. A coarse-graining can be the right causal description, but not by beating the micro. Under one intervention distribution at both levels, no coarse-graining of a transition carries more effective information than its micro ([THEORY-1167](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md)). The ones that lose nothing are exactly causal feature learning's partitions, which merge only micro states with the same interventional effects ([THEORY-1169](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1169.md)). The step from there to "the causes are found at the coarsest such description" is the record's own, in the sense of proportionality. It does not say the macro adds causal information. | Active |
| [CLAIM-498](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-498.md) v2 | Averaging weights within a basin averages features: the network whose weights are the average of several networks in one low-loss basin has, in every layer, the average of their features | The averaging clause of [THEORY-111](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)'s old title, kept as a Proposed claim by the [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) sweep of 2026-10-30 (kind 2) when the eleventh status review's narrowing had dropped it. Zhou et al. (2024), LIT-2646, assert it and measure it for soups of 5 and 10 ViT-B/32 fine-tunes (THEORY-1890); SWA iterates, the other half of its defeater, are not measured. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-499](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-499.md) | The linear barrier left after aligning independently trained networks over the architecture's symmetries rises with depth | The depth clause of [THEORY-112](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md)'s old title, kept as a Proposed claim by the [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) sweep of 2026-10-30 (kind 2) when the eleventh status review's narrowing had dropped it. No source measures or states it for barriers after alignment: it is the record's composition of Entezari et al.'s unaligned depth curves with Ferbach et al.'s compounding width bound. Its defeater is the depth paragraph of the old promote_when. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-500](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-500.md) v2 | The governance-induced kind of frustration is not idle: some failures of an organization's actual updates to meet demands that an admissible update would meet are explained by how influence is allocated, and not by step size, curvature, noise, conditioning or a fixed weighting rule | Split from [CLAIM-357](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) by the eighteenth status review ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [CLAIM-357](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) separates structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and says none of them identifies thwarting. This claim is the thesis that its old defeat condition tested: that the governance-induced kind does work an optimizer analysis does not, because some satisfiable demands go unmet through the allocation of influence. Untested; A39's case study 2 on [CASE-099](../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md) would test it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-501](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-501.md) v2 | Gutt's interpretive resemblance also predicts that judged pragmatic observables beat text similarity, so the central theses' defeat conditions cannot tell the thesis from a relevance-theoretic account either | Split from [CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) by the nineteenth status review ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation) and promoted by the twenty-first, once Gutt's 1989 thesis (LIT-1845) was read. [CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) holds that functional equivalence and a proposition with its force both predict a pass on the central defeat test. This claim adds Gutt's relevance-theoretic account. The book ([LIT-784](../../record/literature.d/LIT-784.md)) stays unread. | Active |
| [CLAIM-502](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-502.md) v2 | Multi-hop delegation can keep an operator's authority exactly independent of its own grants: under leave-one-out damped delegation, which counts the authority reaching each operator only along paths that have not already passed through it, an operator's grants raise the authority of every operator its grantee reaches and leave its own unchanged | A construction that shows [CLAIM-282](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)'s old title false. Compute each operator's authority from A2's damped recursive rule with that operator's own outgoing grants removed. Then authority reaches it along paths of any length, but only along paths that have not passed through it, so nothing it grants can return to it. Its authority is exactly independent of its own grants, and a grant moves authority two hops and more. It does not say the rule conserves authority, that it closes the social route of moving others' grants, or that [CLAIM-375](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md)'s guarantee carries over. | Active |
| [CLAIM-503](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-503.md) v2 | Over finitely many states and finite outcome sets, one experiment is ε-deficient relative to another in every decision problem with losses in [0, 1] exactly when a single Markov kernel brings it within ε in total variation at every state, so the deficiency computed as a linear programme is the least such ε | Le Cam's randomization criterion for finite experiments, uniform in the state, with losses in [0, 1]. The least ε for which some kernel brings M within ε of N in total variation at every state, which [CLAIM-381](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) computes as a linear programme, equals the least ε for which M is ε-deficient relative to N in every finite decision problem. One direction composes N's rule with the kernel; the other is one minimax step over a bilinear objective. At ε = 0 it is the finite Blackwell order ([THEORY-717](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-504](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-504.md) | The strongest operationalization of the functional and relevance-theoretic rivals to the transport structure is a rich contextual baseline of context-response profiles and supervised prediction | Split from [CLAIM-205](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-205.md) by the twenty-first status review ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). The interlocutor's reading of 2026-10-12 proposed it as the fourth row of [CLAIM-202](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md)'s comparison. [CLAIM-205](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-205.md), narrowed, holds that the functional and relevance-theoretic accounts need not fix one context or a static profile; this claim says what their strongest operationalization is. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-505](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-505.md) | A goal's lowered priority under positive affect need not be a weaker hold of the prevailing ordering: on Carver's satisficing account the effort released goes to the goal furthest behind, which the prevailing ordering of the system's states may itself direct | Filed at the twenty-first status review, because the point turned up in three readings of 2026-10-30 ([NOTE-1442](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1442.md), [NOTE-1438](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1438.md), [NOTE-1450](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1450.md)). [CLAIM-468](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-468.md) reads a goal's lowered priority under positive affect as a weaker hold of the prevailing ordering. Carver's own account, as his group restates it, reads the same shift as a reordering of priorities among goals, satisficing across them, which the prevailing ordering may itself direct. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-506](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-506.md) v2 | The split of the last eukaryotic common ancestor's central carbon metabolism, archaeal enzymes in the cytosol and alphaproteobacterial ones in the mitochondrion, does not single out syntrophy: a host that kept its own archaeal glycolysis and took up a bacterium with a TCA cycle leaves it whether the partnership began in syntrophy or by engulfment by an already complex host, and what the split counts against is a host whose carbon metabolism was replaced by the symbiont's | Split from [THEORY-1109](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [THEORY-1109](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) reports what Santana-Molina and colleagues find and that they read it as support for syntrophy; this claim is the record's judgement that the split cannot carry that reading. | Active |
| [CLAIM-507](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-507.md) v2 | On WMT22 News MQM, xCOMET's error spans are more coherent with its own regression scores than either is with expert judgement: the agreement between its heads is coherence between two outputs of one model, and adds little to what the spans' own agreement with experts shows | The record's reading of Guerreiro et al.'s Table 5, split from [THEORY-1134](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1134.md) when the twenty-second status review narrowed it to the measurements and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 2). An instance of [CLAIM-496](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md)'s distinction between coherence and fidelity. The statistics compared differ (Pearson between heads; Kendall and F1 against humans), and converted to one scale the gap is smaller than it looks. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-508](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-508.md) v2 | Gene ancestries alone cannot tell a symbiotic partner from a source of transferred genes: a partner whose genes were mostly lost, replaced or spread thin would leave the diffuse trace that Tobiasson and colleagues read as piecemeal transfer, and Bernabeu and colleagues concede that their donor signals say nothing of the kind of interaction | Split from [THEORY-1104](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [THEORY-1104](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) reports Tobiasson and colleagues' reading of diffuse bacterial genes as transfer; [THEORY-1105](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1105.md) reports Bernabeu and colleagues' concession about their own donors. This claim is what the record draws from both. | Active |
| [CLAIM-509](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-509.md) v2 | Stem lengths alone do not establish an order of acquisition in eukaryogenesis, neither Pittis and Gabaldón's late mitochondrion nor Bernabeu and colleagues' transfer waves: normalized stem length measures time only if rates before and after LECA are proportional, it shortens as closer relatives are sampled, the alphaproteobacterial separation from other bacteria rests on P = 0.044, and on Tobiasson and colleagues' data it does not behave as a clock | Split from [THEORY-1102](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1102.md) and [THEORY-1101](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). The two readings, now Active, report what the papers find; this claim is the record's judgement of what stem lengths can establish. | Active |
| [CLAIM-510](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-510.md) | Measurement can establish, and not only estimate, a correspondence among local descriptions: some correspondences that measurement estimates can be checked against evidence the measurement did not itself produce | The clause [CLAIM-471](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md) dropped when the twenty-fourth status review narrowed "establish" to "estimate" ([ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 2). It is the record's own wording, and no source asserts it. [CLAIM-143](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md)'s order of tests needs it to be possible, since the order asks for correspondences that are independently validated. No held case meets it yet. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md) v5 | A self-maintaining organization ought to preserve its corrigibility | The proposition the owner asked about at U24 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "have we established ... why/that corrigibility is desirable?" Not claimed. The record's constructions of maintained correction do not establish it ([ARG-042](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-042.md), Rejected), and its value is conditional on objectives, uncertainty and cost ([CLAIM-520](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md)). A24's answer: "We have not established that corrigibility is unconditionally desirable." Filed because the owner asked, so it marks a real boundary. It would be argued from a declared standard, which is where [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) and [QUESTION-129](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md) ask. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-512](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-512.md) v5 | The diachronic thesis faces two objections: a dilemma, that read narrowly it fails for judgments not about any organization's continuation, such as that suffering is bad, and read broadly every judgment is met vacuously as a preference between continuations unless the organizational description adds causal specificity, transfer or counterfactual discrimination; and a distinction, that evaluating a history is not prescribing its continuation, so a judgment can be determinate with no future transformation fixed | The objection to [CLAIM-518](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md), put by the assistant itself in A26 §6 and A27 §10 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "If we call every difference between possible worlds a change in some organization, then all normative judgments can be represented in these terms without learning much", and "A judgment that suffering is bad, for instance, is not obviously about organizational persistence". Conceded by CLAIM-518 at its versions 2 and 3. Its broad horn is the condition CLAIM-608 must meet. A27's three tests are the form an answer would take. | Active |
| [CLAIM-513](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-513.md) | Across a family of goals, a world model is not an optional explanation of competent behaviour: in a fully observed, finite, communicating, stationary environment, a goal-conditioned policy within a factor 1 − δ of optimal on every composite goal of depth n fixes every transition probability to within √(2P(1 − P)/((n − 1)(1 − δ))), so observers reading the same policy must ascribe the same world model; what it leaves open is whether a predictive component is realized inside the agent, since a lookup table over histories and goals has the same policy | From the reading of Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt ([LIT-1891](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), [NOTE-1469](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md)), registered as the objection to watch against the owner's U20 thesis [CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md). It defeats that thesis's functional reading only. The thesis's defeated_if is not met: the theorem holds "regardless of ... architecture", makes no matched-resource comparison and no intervention on internals, and its authors say the map runs "from the agent's policy rather than its activations". Within its scope, though, calling a world model an explanatory attribution is too weak. The bound was re-derived and checked against an adversarial agent. | Active |
| [CLAIM-514](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) | World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded capabilities for producing and using predictions about an environment's possibilities and consequences, each relative to a declared family of questions; a world model in the representational sense is one possible realization of them, competent behaviour can determine environmental structure without identifying any internal mechanism, and producing, maintaining and revising world-modeling capabilities are further achievements, not prerequisites of agency in general | The owner's preferred formulation at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). It joins the world-model thesis, which holds that behaviour does not identify a mechanism, and its counter from Richens et al., which holds that behaviour across goals determines the dynamics. Both are kept, with each stated about a different notion of world model. It "integrates the Richens result rather than rejecting it, preserves [the] original critique of folk-model attributions, and connects both to the larger Nucleation program." Proposed: a definition and an organizing thesis, with the study [CASE-187](../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md) as its test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-515](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) v2 | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." It was drawn from the world-model case ([CLAIM-514](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md)) and judged "sufficiently general—and sufficiently testable—that it deserves an explicit place in Nucleation's research program". Interpretive: its instances are demonstrated case by case, and the generalization is not. | Active |
| [CLAIM-516](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md) | Where every constraint capacity turns over at a positive rate and is produced only by others, with no basal production and production vanishing as its producers do, capacities whose production graph is acyclic all decay to zero: a capacity that persists needs a productive cycle among its ancestors, and removing a feedback edge set extinguishes every capacity; a cycle is necessary and not sufficient, and a one-member cycle is not closure | From A10 §1 and §5A of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), after the owner's "try to progress the theoretical program". | [CLAIM-517](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-517.md) v2 | A successor regulator keeps a viable set positively invariant if, at every boundary context, its response distribution is within γ/L in total variation of a regulator that certifies inward margin γ, the dynamics being L-Lipschitz in that distribution; an average distillation loss certifies this only through coverage of the boundary contexts, so fidelity measured in ordinary operation certifies nothing about viability | From A16 §4 and §5 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), the owner having quoted its conclusion at U17: "preserving a regulator's response distribution sufficiently accurately can guarantee preservation of a physical organization's viability". | [CLAIM-518](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md) v4 | Normative judgments about an organization's continuity, reform or obligations can depend on diachronic relations that descriptions of present states or terminal outcomes do not show, so specifying the relevant relations and histories can be necessary to apply them adequately; which continuations ought to follow is a further normative question, not a prerequisite of every normative judgment | From the owner's observation at U26 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), "normative judgements are only cognizable when they are relative to a judgement of whether some organization should persist or change", as narrowed at the owner's review the same day. What survives is that judgments about continuity, reform and obligation can need histories that present states and outcomes do not show. | [CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". | [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) v7 | Recovery under interventions on state cannot show where maintenance is realized: an outside controller that measures the constraint capacities and supplies the internal production law as state feedback yields the same trajectory under every perturbation of state, damage and recovery included, even with every capacity observed exactly; only interventions on the production mechanisms, relative to a declared boundary, separate the two | From A10 §4 (its Proposition 5) of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) v13 | For a normatively relevant discrepancy to change what an organization does, three distinct achievements are needed and any can fail while the others hold: legibility, by which the discrepancy becomes recognizable; volitional efficacy, by which a corresponding demand can move action; and correctability, by which a fitting revision can be carried out within deadline and resources; none establishes that the demand or the revision is justified, and whether the norm-satisfying histories the agent can still realize are empty depends partly on what its earlier actions destroyed | The owner's synthesis at review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-524](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-524.md) | Whether functionally equivalent realizations are connected depends on which paths are admissible: for f = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ with nonnegative weights, (1, 1, 0, 0) and (0, 0, 1, 1) are joined by a curve along which f stays 1 though the straight line between them falls to ½, and under any resource budget below √2 times the endpoints' cost no path with f = 1 joins them | From the owner's remark at U17 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), that the reconstruction fibres "reminds me of loss landscape connected mode stuff (which might just be a consequence of high dimensional geometry? ... probably already discussed on the nucleation record)". | [CLAIM-525](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-525.md) v2 | Information in the sense the Simondonian readings give it, a disparity whose resolution reorders the system that takes it up, is in the line's terms a change in the interpreter or in the questions receivers can decide, not evidence about a fixed situation, so Blackwell's order leaves it out by construction and the two accounts are not rivals | The record's placing, on 2026-10-31, of the information concept in the Simondon readings (Iliadis 2013; Bencherki and Iliadis 2021; Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy 2024) against the line's Blackwell treatment.
