| [CLAIM-526](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) v2 | Describing persons and organizations as coexisting levels of one process removes the question of how already-constituted agents add up to a collective, but not the question of levels: whether a collective variable has dynamics of its own, closed against the activity that realizes it, can be decided on a process description that presupposes no agents, is sometimes decided no, and a closed collective variable can be an aggregate that coexists with its realization while keeping none of its members' distinctions | Filed on reading Bencherki & Iliadis 2021 and Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024, who hold that the "scaling up" problem "vanishes the moment communication is viewed eventfully" ([LIT-1902](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364) because persons and organizations are "different informational levels that preserve all the characteristics of their organized components" ([LIT-1922](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), ms. p. 21, proposition 2). The record's closure results show what survives. What vanishes is the picture of agents adding up. What remains is whether a higher variable runs on its own, which is a question about variables and is decidable. The record's own case of a closed collective variable is a sum, an aggregate, that coexists with its units, so "stages or coexisting levels" is not a dichotomy. It does not say that the agent picture is right, or that organizations are aggregates of members. | Active |
| [CLAIM-527](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-527.md) v2 | Viable reach, valence and emotion are three quantities in an organization, not one: an emotion is a claim to precedence, system valence is movement along the ordering that wins the negotiation, and a change in what the organization can viably reach is neither, so an organization can run ahead along its prevailing ordering while its viable reach contracts | Filed 2026-10-31 from the readings of Massumi and McKim (2009) and Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024). Massumi's affect is a transition in a body's capacitation, augmented or diminished, and the parent paper defines agency as its augmenting half. The record's affect line reads emotion as a claim to precedence (Frijda) and system valence as movement along what wins the negotiation; neither is a change in what can be done. This claim names the third quantity, viable reach, and says it can move against valence. It does not say that Massumi's capacitation is viable reach, or that more reach is better. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-528](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-528.md) v2 | That a mechanism realizes a capacity can mean that the capacity is produced through it over time or that the capacity consists in it at a time, and interventions show only the first: a pathway whose disabling changes the capacity after a delay is a cause, can be intervened on surgically, and can be located relative to a declared boundary, whereas every intervention on a capacity that consists in its parts also changes some part along another path, so that relation is underdetermined by intervention data and is inferred by abduction or from simultaneity and settled parthood; and which of the two a given dependence is depends on the time resolution at which a description treats the parts' response as instantaneous | Filed on reading the fat-handedness debate after Craver: Baumgartner & Gebharter 2016, Baumgartner & Casini 2017 and Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel 2020. It says what their result does and does not reach in the record. [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s conclusion is causal and is left standing; [CLAIM-515](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md)'s "realized", read synchronically, is not shown by discriminating interventions; and the debate's own line between causation and constitution, simultaneity, moves with the time scale, as [CLAIM-480](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md)'s chain shows. | [CLAIM-529](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) v4 | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, individuating it by a different relation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). Their abstract says transitions in individuality are hard to describe without circularity, since the features used are products of the transition, and claims a non-circular description that the body never argues. The body holds the parts of an answer, and they are of two kinds. Criteria on interactions (per-member accounting of benefit, entrenchment order, knockout of interaction types, release from a scaffold) can test a declared candidate without assuming it is a unit ([CLAIM-405](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md)), and the scaffold test needs the declared boundary ([CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)). Criteria on members' attitudes toward the group (shared goal, belonging, focal goal of sustaining it) individuate constitutively, which is not the non-circular route and is unavailable for organisms without such attitudes. It does not say the paper argues this, and it leaves the presupposed lower-level units where the paper leaves them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-530](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md) v3 | Where maintenance is realized is a question of constitutive relevance only through its parthood condition: an internal producer and an outside controller supplying the same production law as state feedback meet mutual manipulability's two manipulability conditions identically, since disabling or stimulating either changes the maintained capacities and intervening on the capacities changes the activity of either, so what puts one inside and the other outside is parthood, a boundary the experiments presuppose and do not find | The record's join of [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) with the mechanist account of constitution, from Craver and Bechtel's admission that interlevel experiments are symmetrical and show componency only prima facie ([THEORY-1287](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md)). The criterion is cited as Baumgartner and Gebharter state it (LIT-1934, p. 8, read in full in NOTE-1493); Craver's own texts stay unread. It does not say no criterion can draw the boundary. | [CLAIM-531](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) v4 | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure. | [CLAIM-532](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) v7 | An unresolved discrepancy is an occasion for self-formation, the transformation dimension of a will-organization, and not a guarantee of it; it suffices for self-formation that the agent's own activity on such a discrepancy produce a maintained capacity, either a new distinction, its policy coming to depend on a feature of its situation it did not depend on, or a new channel, the outcomes it can reach under its own policy growing, that outlasts the discrepancy and serves a class of later ones, as shown by transfer to discrepancies of the same class after the inducing conditions are gone and by interventions on the processes that produce the capacity while it forms | The positive account A33 §7 offered, at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), sharpened by the reader of U32–U33 so that it can fail. The steps A33 chains, discrepancy to discrimination to response to maintained capacity to revised governance, are not a sequence ([CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)). | [CLAIM-534](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) v2 | A plural will's motivational integration, a dimension of freedom of will the record names and leaves unanalysed, is the extent to which the demands it maintains are jointly met, within tolerances it can recognize, across the contexts where they interact, and kept so under its own dynamics; it is neither agreement among the demands nor the dominance of one, and its parts come apart: realizability (the tolerance frontier), realization (governance frustration), maintenance (viability) and the allocation of the tolerance each demand gives up | A positive account, filed at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "are there any positive accounts or even just hypotheses we should consider documenting on the record (even if just as proposals)?" | [CLAIM-535](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md) v7 | An organization that acts on what it observes has a policy acceptable in every circumstance exactly when, for each observation, the circumstances it cannot tell apart share an acceptable action; so every circumstance having an acceptable action does not give a policy, a finer observation never removes one, and where acceptable actions overlap the coarsest observations that suffice are several and incomparable, so which distinctions must be made legible depends on which acceptable action the organization commits to | A33 §4 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's U33 request for positive accounts, with A30 §2's example and A32's Claim B. | [CLAIM-536](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md) v3 | A categorical model of perspectives and an LDA-style model differ in where the mixture lives: the first draws every act's perspective from one fixed categorical distribution, the second gives each episode its own mixture, drawn from a Dirichlet, and draws each act from it; the Dirichlet is a distribution over mixtures, not the perspectives themselves, and with symmetric concentration a over K perspectives two acts in one episode share a perspective with probability (a + 1)/(Ka + 1) against 1/K across episodes, so the concentration runs from one perspective per episode, as in persona selection (a → 0), to a fresh independent draw for every act (a → ∞) | The owner's U12 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), stated precisely: "H1 isn't LDA like though. that's my point. it's a categorical distribution. the topics in H@ are the dirichlet distribution which parameterizes the categorical distribution, which is what distinguishes H2 from H1 and why H2 is an LDA." | [CLAIM-537](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md) v2 | In tolerance-bounded compatibility on a graph with disturbed offsets, \|Dx − a₀ − w\| ≤ δ for \|w_e\| ≤ η_e, a compatible configuration exists for every disturbance exactly when \|cᵀa₀\| + Σ η_e\|c_e\| ≤ Σ δ_e\|c_e\| on every cycle, and one configuration serves every disturbance exactly when η ≤ δ and \|cᵀa₀\| ≤ Σ(δ_e − η_e)\|c_e\|; an agent that chooses its configuration from what it observes needs the second condition within each class of disturbances it cannot tell apart, so whether a compatible state can be selected lies between the two and depends on what the agent can read | A30 §§2–3 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's "keep going", with the second and third conditions derived by the reader of U30–U31 and checked by simulation (500 random instances, no mismatch). | [CLAIM-538](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md) | On a finite graph of contexts whose overlaps carry preferred real offsets a and tolerances δ_e ≥ 0, an assignment within every tolerance, \|Dx − a\| ≤ δ, exists exactly when no cycle's holonomy exceeds the sum of its tolerances; with every δ_e > 0 the least uniform enlargement of the tolerances that admits one is the largest ratio, over simple cycles, of holonomy to summed tolerance, so the obstruction is certified by a cycle; the feasible allocations of tolerance depend on the offsets only through their class in H¹, so local adjustment can move a mismatch among the overlaps of a cycle and never remove it; and an evaluation that omits one overlap of every witnessing cycle reports a compatibility that does not hold | The owner's U27 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), "compatibility of tolerance bounds", with U28's pointer to the record's sheaf tools, worked out at A28 §3 and A29 §§3–4, 7 and A32's Claim A. The feasibility criterion is the classical feasible-differential theorem of network flows (Rockafellar 1984; no checked identifier, not registered), and the ratio is LP duality, so the result is granted, not the record's discovery. What the record adds is the reading: the frontier is an invariant of the obstruction class, governance chooses where on it the mismatch falls, and omission can fake compatibility. Checked by linear programming against brute-force cycle enumeration on random graphs. | Active |
| [CLAIM-539](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-539.md) v2 | Jennings's attention as the source of a free will has Frankfurt's two-level architecture with its upper level changed from an attitude to a process: the whole collection of an agent's interests, prioritizing, settles which first-order interest becomes effective, as a second-order volition does for Frankfurt, but by metacontrol and not by endorsement; so it inherits unchanged the objection that a manipulated organization can meet the condition, and what it adds to Frankfurt is that the process forms new interests and is a contextually emergent cause | The owner's U14 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "would it be fair to say Jennings theory is Frankfurt with a hat on?" Answered from [CLAIM-122](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md)'s note of 2026-10-18, which separates higher-order volition, an attitude about what should be effective, from metacontrol, the machinery that alters what becomes effective. First filed as a note on [CLAIM-122](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md), since the paper was unread. | [CLAIM-540](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-540.md) | The persistence a Dirichlet–categorical hierarchy gives a run of selections is an observer's learning about a fixed mixture, not a change in what selects: under a uniform prior an observed first choice raises the predicted chance of repeating it from 1/2 to 2/3, while the same choice forced leaves it at 1/2, so the hierarchy's reinforcement is not evidence of self-formation or of a maintained will-organization, which need the mixture itself to change under the choice | A13 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), answering the owner's U13, what the Dirichlet–categorical reading implies for Jennings's attention as the source of a free will. A13: "Self-formation requires a causal update, not merely a posterior update in the observer." Correct, short and not held. Rechecked here by simulation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-541](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-541.md) v3 | Wu-wei is better read as control placed and timed where a system's own dynamics do most of the work than as the absence of control: Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control of chaos is a formal instance, in which small perturbations timed by the system's own wandering hold it on an unstable orbit, and the control, though small, continues for as long as the orbit is held; so reported effortlessness has at least three distinct sources, no conflict to override, conflict settled cheaply by learned accommodation, and conflict met as it arises by small well-timed feedback, which may feel alike and differ in mechanism | The owner's U17 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), quoting A16 on Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control: "that's very wu-wei". | [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) v5 | Where every replacement part is supplied from outside, an organization can become independent of what founded it but never of what feeds it: with damage at rate d and supplied repair at rate ρs the intact fraction holds at ρs/(ρs + d), needs a supply growing as θ/(1 − θ) times the damage rate to hold a share θ, and decays as e^(−dt) once the supply stops, as DNA origami that self-heals from a strand pool and origami that replicates from supplied monomers both illustrate | The assistant's, on the owner's invitation of 2026-11-05 to add readings and claims to the DNA origami filing. | [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v10 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely only if it started a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, was large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, outlasted the threat it stood in for, and left the work to the party throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept up after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement; support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, but meeting them all is not enough, since support can carry a function nobody names before withdrawal; and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions are needed for it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-077](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)) and returned to CLAIM on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated. | Active |
| [CLAIM-601](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) v4 | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time | The assistant's, after the owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding, that deprivation produces short-sighted choices, as decision-making under a resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the decision making process." Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Survival, the objective deprivation makes binding, needs a deeper buffer than expected wealth. | [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) v5 | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. | [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v8 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) v3 | Where each damaged part of a structure is repaired by drawing on a flux at a rate proportional to the structure's intact share, as a flame's upkeep is, it has an ignition threshold below which it goes out with the supply still on, a supply level below which it collapses rather than declines, and an outage after which restoring the supply does not relight it; repair supplied at a rate set by the supply alone, whatever the structure's state, has none of the three | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to connect [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)'s supplied maintenance to the record's dissipative structures. [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) modelled only the first. The second is modelled by letting uptake from the flux scale with the intact share: dI/dt = −dI + κsI²(1 − I). With d = 0.2 and κs = 2 the structure holds 0.887, as supplied repair at ρs = 1.575 does, but it goes out from 0.10 with the supply on, collapses when the supply falls below 40 % of its level, and after an outage longer than about 10.3 time units does not relight when the supply returns. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-605](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) v5 | Where capacity is learned by doing, decays with disuse and needs capacity already present to grow, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold | The assistant's, filling gaps the supplied-maintenance filing left, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to "proceed systematically filling all of those identified gaps". [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) modelled crowding out with no threshold, so capacity always regrew from a seed. Its own limits named the threshold case, Azam et al.'s trap. The model gives three results. Support that does all the work has a deadline: after ln(0.7/0.276)/0.3 = 3.10 time units capacity has crossed the threshold, and withdrawal no longer restores it. Tapering such support is worse the slower it is: from C = 0.45 under support doing 95 % of the work, an abrupt cut recovers, a taper over 5 periods recovers, and any taper longer than 9.13 periods traps the party. Capacity-first support needs no taper, since it withdraws itself, but it cannot lift a party already below the threshold. | [CLAIM-606](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) v5 | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on | The assistant's, after the owner's hunch that "the physics/dynamics of soliton formation could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions about individuation and persistence".   supply. They come in a family set by their initial data, and they keep

  Their shape is "predetermined by the equation parameters, rather than

- Topological solitons carry a charge that continuous change cannot
  remove.

| [CLAIM-706](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-706.md) v4 | Execution impedance, independent constraint and intervention opportunity vary independently: an institution can cut the time and cost of execution while reducing, preserving or expanding others' opportunities to intervene, and can keep a step the executor cannot pass alone that opens no opportunity at all, so the three must be assessed separately, and whether the owner's procedural friction is impedance or constraint is left open | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse", accepted by the owner on 2026-11-16, and rewritten at the review of 2026-11-16. Simon's near-decomposability ([THEORY-661](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md)) is about interaction strengths: interactions within subsystems much stronger than between them. | [CLAIM-865](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-865.md) | Where a support acts on an assembly only by changing its transition rates and is withdrawn for good, the drop in the chance of completing when it is withdrawn at a state equals the expected total, along the course the supported assembly would take from that state, of how much the support changes each rate times how much the unsupported chance of completing turns on that step; for a support that holds a nucleus this is the nucleus's fragility times its worth, so the assembly becomes independent of the support before it is complete only where what it has built holds the nucleus or no longer needs it | The assistant's, from carrying out [LEAD-095](../../record/leads.d/LEAD-095.md). A's measure for [QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) is D(s) = q_supported(s) − q_withdrawn(s). On the transient states, Q_S(q_S − q_0) = −(Q_S − Q_0)q_0, so D(s) is the expected integral, along the supported path from s, of the support's rate changes weighted by the unsupported committor's differences across them. That is a standard perturbation identity for absorption probabilities; its use here is the record's. Three things follow. The chance after withdrawal depends on the state reached alone, so all the support leaves behind is the state. | [CLAIM-902](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-902.md) v2 | Under multiplicative co-occurrence with any implication structure among binary attributes and positive strengths, every attribute is an exact linear readout of the full-rank PMI embedding; on a balanced tree the PMI eigenvectors are branch contrasts whose eigenvalues fall strictly with depth, so a truncated embedding keeps exactly the shallow attributes and merges siblings below the cut | The model of [THEORY-185](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-185.md) with its independence dropped: binary attributes closed upward under any implication order, each shared attribute multiplying co-occurrence by a positive factor, so the PMI is X Λ Xᵀ plus affine terms. Every attribute is read out exactly, by an affine map, from the full-rank spectral embedding, and the recovered incidence and its concept lattice equal the generating ones. What implication changes is the spectrum. On a balanced b-ary tree, the eigenvectors are branch contrasts rather than one per attribute. So a rank-(b^K − 1) embedding reads out exactly the attributes of depth at most K. | [CLAIM-1046](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1046.md) v2 | The observational partitions a family of affordable probes induces are not the lattice of possible decompositions: the map from probe subsets to partitions sends a union of families to the common refinement of their partitions, but an intersection of families to a partition that can be strictly coarser than the finest common coarsening, so its image is closed under meets and not under joins, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members against the Bell number of partitions of the configurations | A15 §2 says "the lattice of all partitions of Ω is generally much larger than the set of partitions realizable by our affordable probes", and that the probe lattice "is a structure of which distinctions our methods support", not of selves. For fixed configurations Ω and fixed response laws, let π(Q) be the partition of Ω into classes no probe in Q separates. Then π(Q1 ∪ Q2) is the meet (common refinement) of π(Q1) and π(Q2), while π(Q1 ∩ Q2) is at least as coarse as their join and can be strictly coarser. So π is order-reversing and meet-preserving, its image is a meet-closed part of the partition lattice and need not be a sublattice, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members, against Bell(\|Ω\|) partitions (32 against 115,975 for m = 5 and \|Ω\| = 10).
